| 9 | Victor Mesa Jr. | TB | OF | 43% | 4% |
| 10 | Leo Bernal | STL | C | 35% | 3% |
| 11 | Javier Sanoja | MIA | 2B,3B,SS,OF | 62% | 3% |
(+/-) is the % of leagues the player was added to in the previous week
It’s possible that attraction towards Ryan Johnson this weekend relates to dynasty and keeper formats, and not his start in Seattle this week. Johnson has limited run damage over his last nine starts, since August 6, posting a 2.39 ERA, but with an xFIP (5.01) nearly double the mark. Johnson is more of a 4.25-4.50 ERA guy than a sub-3.00 ERA one, as his 90.9% LOB and .229 BABIP portends.
Perhaps a similar mindset applies to folks who scooped up Jack Perkins, who pitched two quality starts on the road against the Rays (6.2 IP – 4 H – 0 ER – 1 BB – 8 K) and the Guardians (6 IP – 5 H – 1 ER – 0 BB – 4 K), flashing some of his upside and future potential. Perkins has had a difficult season (5.90 ERA, but a 4.16 xFIP, 1.45 WHIP) and will be a tough streamer at home in Sacramento next season, but the strikeouts (25.2%) should always be there.
Andrew Alvarez should have a rotation spot with the Nationals next season. He has been outstanding since the All-Star break, posting a 2.44 ERA (3.30 FIP, 4.02 xFIP) with a 1.10 WHIP and a 22.7% strikeout rate, though he wasn’t able to secure a win in any of those 10 starts. Alvarez won’t be a particularly coveted target in drafts next season, but should have a NFBC ADP somewhere in the 250-325 overall range. He may be a consideration in NL-only keeper leagues with deep benches and five-plus keepers.
Bold Predictions for Week 27
Gavin Williams and Jacob Misiorowski finish the season tied for the MLB lead in strikeouts with 255. Williams punches out 11 and Misiorowski, eight.
JR Ritchie steps up for his two starts and has a Jack Perkins Week 26 type week, helping managers win league titles.
Cade Cavalli twirls a gem in Detroit this week and pulls his 3.02 ERA under 3.00 to end the season. Cavalli will have a top-60 ADP in 2027.
Jo Adell takes advantage of four left-handed starters this week and earns seven RBIs to reach 100, after falling two RBIs short last season.
One of Cristian Javier or Yusei Kikuchi will remind why streaming pitchers in Sutter Health Park, even if part of a two-step, is a mistake.
Miguel Vargas and Colson Montgomery hit three home runs each this week and the White Sox score the most runs in Week 27.
The Houston Astros win the NL West and knock the Texas Rangers out of playoff contention.
I hope you enjoyed my column this season and that you found it helpful, or at least entertaining and informative. Stay tuned for more from me next week as we hit the offseason streets. Best of luck this final week!
Vlad writes for RotoGraphs and is the head of fantasy baseball content at FTN Fantasy. He is a Tout Wars Expert League champ, member of the CDM Fantasy Sports Hall of Fame and has been nominated for FSWA writing awards six times. Vlad has been playing fantasy baseball since 1995, winning 42 NFBC leagues since 2012 and ranking in the top percentile in NFBC’s Online Championship contest (33% win rate, 52% cash rate; 64 leagues). Much to the chagrin of his colleagues and most baseball aficionados, Vlad is a lifelong Dodgers fan who claims his first gut call at age 9 was Kirk Gibson’s 1988 World Series home run. You can follow him on X and BlueSky @RotoGut.

item.title: [NBC Sports Boston] Who matters most for Red Sox in playoffs? We ranked the top 10
item.dc:creator: Justin Leger
item.description: The Boston Red Sox have officially clinched a postseason berth, completing one of the most improbable turnarounds in MLB history. But the real test begins next week. After falling to the New York Yankees in last year’s Wild Card Series, Boston is looking to make a deeper October run this time around, and it looks like the Yankees will once again stand in the way. It’s been a total team effort for Boston all season long, but the playoffs are where stars emerge and the margin for error becomes raz
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox have officially clinched a postseason berth, completing one of the most improbable turnarounds in MLB history.
But the real test begins next week. After falling to the New York Yankees in last year’s Wild Card Series, Boston is looking to make a deeper October run this time around, and it looks like the Yankees will once again stand in the way.
It’s been a total team effort for Boston all season long, but the playoffs are where stars emerge and the margin for error becomes razor thin. While nearly everyone on the postseason roster will play a role, we’ve narrowed it down to the 10 players who could have the biggest impact on how far this team goes.
Here are the 10 most important -- not necessarily the best -- Red Sox players for the 2026 playoffs:
1. Payton Tolle, SP
What a difference a year makes. Last year, Tolle experienced growing pains in his first MLB stint and pitched just 1/3 of an inning in the Wild Card Series at Yankee Stadium. This time, he's coming off an exceptional rookie campaign with a chance to start Game 1 in the Bronx.
Tolle will enter the postseason with momentum on his side. The 23-year-old tallied 12 strikeouts while allowing just one run in six innings against Baltimore. He followed that up with six shutout innings against Kansas City, including an immaculate inning to begin the game.
If Tolle continues to perform at this level, he'll give the Red Sox another frontline starter who can match up against other teams' aces. He's the pitcher with the greatest opportunity to change the trajectory of this postseason roster.
If the Red Sox make a deep postseason run, it'll be because their rookie left-hander delivered each time he took the mound on the big stage.
2. Sonny Gray, SP
We're sticking with pitching, because pitching is what propelled this Red Sox club to a postseason berth in the first place.
If Tolle is No. 1, it would be silly not to put Gray right behind him at No. 2. The 36-year-old veteran stabilized the rotation in the wake of Garrett Crochet's injury. He was signed to be the No. 3 starter behind Crochet and Ranger Suarez, but he performed like an ace with a 17-5 record and a 2.82 ERA in 28 starts.
Now, Boston will lean on Gray and his big-game experience to lead the staff in October. Even if he doesn't start Game 1 of the Wild Card Series, Gray will play a huge role in any postseason success.
3. Roman Anthony, LF/DH
The top position player on our list is the 22-year-old many expected to anchor Boston's lineup and produce an MVP-caliber season in 2026. Instead, Anthony spent most of the year on the injured list and has largely struggled in the 50 games he's been healthy. We know what the former No. 1 prospect is capable of, however, and he'll significantly raise the Red Sox' ceiling if he plays up to his potential in the postseason.
The Red Sox will lean heavily on their pitching staff throughout the playoffs, but Anthony is the X-factor in the lineup. This is a completely different club when he gets hot.
All it will take is a signature postseason moment for Red Sox fans to forget about the disappointing start to Anthony's young career.
4. Ranger Suarez, SP
OK, back to pitching. A big reason the Red Sox signed Suarez to a five-year, $130 million contract in free agency is that he has a stellar postseason track record. The 31-year-old boasts a 1.48 ERA across 11 playoff appearances (eight starts) with the Philadelphia Phillies.
The only reason he isn't higher on this list is we project him to be the No. 3 starter, which means we won't even see him if the Sox get swept out of the Wild Card Series. If Boston advances, another strong postseason from Suarez will be critical for their World Series chances.
5. Wilyer Abreu, RF
Abreu is one of Boston's best all-around players, but he's a streaky hitter. The Red Sox' mediocre offense can't afford for him to go cold in the postseason, so he's an incredibly important piece if they hope to make a deep run.
When he's hot, Abreu's bat is elite. He leads the American League with 36 doubles along with 24 homers in 151 games.
As important as his bat will be, Abreu's Gold Glove defense in right field will also be a difference-maker. Postseason games can come down to one defensive miscue, and Abreu has earned a reputation as one of the best defensive right fielders in baseball.
If Abreu can give the Red Sox consistent at-bats and quality defense, he can quietly become one of the most impactful players on the roster over an entire series.
6. Willson Contreras, 1B
We've got the Venezuelan sluggers back-to-back. Contreras has been the Red Sox' most consistent bat all season, and he'll be leaned on heavily in the heart of the lineup throughout the playoffs.
Unlike most of Boston's lineup, Contreras will enter the Wild Card Series with plenty of postseason experience. He won a World Series with the 2016 Chicago Cubs and has 30 playoff games under his belt in total.
With a team-high 27 homers, Contreras will be counted on to supply the Red Sox lineup with power throughout their playoff run. If he goes cold, there will be even more pressure on guys like Anthony, Abreu, and the player who's next up on our list to get runs on the board.
7. Adley Rutschman, C
Rutschman will need to step it up offensively, but his importance goes beyond his bat because of his position. One could argue the role he plays behind the plate is even more crucial.
As Boston's starting catcher, Rutschman will be responsible for managing the pitching staff through almost every postseason game, meaning he'll be involved on almost every pitch thrown. There's also a significant downgrade at catcher if he goes down with an injury, with only Connor Wong and Mickey Gasper as his potential backups.
For the Red Sox to make it far, Rutschman has to be more than just a productive hitter; he must also work seamlessly with the rotation and bullpen while living up to his reputation as one of the best defensive backstops in the league.
8. Aroldis Chapman, CP
Having a closer who can slam the door shut gives clubs a huge advantage come postseason time. The Red Sox are fortunate to have arguably the best of the bunch.
While Chapman wasn't otherworldly in 2026 like he was in 2025, he still was elite with a 1.95 ERA in 52 appearances. He'll look to limit free passes after watching his walk rate jump from 2.2 to 4.1 BB/9 over last year. If he does that, Boston can effectively shorten games by having him available for the ninth inning. He can also single-handedly lose games, automatically making him one of the club's most important players for the postseason.
9. Garrett Whitlock, RP
Boston's bullpen is perhaps its biggest strength heading into the postseason, and that's because of the Whitlock/Chapman combo at the back end. Whitlock has been an elite set-up man with a 1.75 ERA and 0.877 WHIP across 53 appearances this season.
Starters typically have shorter outings in the playoffs, so we could see the Red Sox turn to Whitlock early and often throughout October if they advance past the Wild Card Series. He's the reliever Boston will count on to mow down the heart of an opposing lineup in a high-leverage situation. That could be the difference between a win and a loss, and that's why Whitlock makes the top 10 over some other very important players.
10. Ceddanne Rafaela, CF
Rafaela rounds out our top 10 most important Red Sox players for the postseason, but don't let his ranking fool you. With elite defense in center field and a bat that made a significant leap this season, he can be considered another X-factor for this club in the playoffs.
If Boston makes a deep run, there's a good chance we'll get at least one signature Rafaela moment. The 26-year-old has a knack for coming up big in the clutch, whether it's with a timely extra-base hit or a mind-blowing catch in center field.
Rafaela's glaring absence during his time on the injured list with a quad injury has highlighted his importance to this club. If he's back to full strength in time for the playoffs, that'll give the Red Sox a major boost.
Honorable mentions: 3B Caleb Durbin, SS Trevor Story, LF/DH Jarren Duran, RP Erik Miller, RP Tyron Guerrero, P Brayan Bello and P Jake Bennett.
They didn't crack the top 10, but that doesn't mean they won't have huge roles in October.
Durbin completely changes the outlook of the offense when he's hitting. He's also been an elite defensive third baseman all season long.
Story has been one of Boston's best hitters since returning from the injured list. There's no guarantee that'll carry over into the playoffs, but he'll at least have to be adequate defensively as the team's starting shortstop.
Duran had a 2026 to forget, and with Anthony in left field and Mickey Gasper likely at DH, he'll probably spend a fair amount of time on the bench. Still, he's the type of player who can change a game with one swing, and his speed is a huge factor.
Miller and Guerrero will have major roles at the back end of the bullpen. Bello (if he makes the roster) and Bennett will be leaned on as bulk relievers. Miller has struggled lately, Guerrero is returning from injury, Bello is unproven in the playoffs, and we haven't seen Bennett come out of the 'pen.

by Chris Schommer | Red Sox Correspondent |
Patrick Sandoval allowed five earned runs on four hits and two walks while striking out five over seven innings in Sunday's loss to the Rays.
Fantasy Impact:
Sandoval has struggled to miss opposing bats of late, allowing three earned runs or more in each of his last four trips to the mound. The left-hander remains one of the more dismal arms as part of an otherwise stable Red Sox rotation for manager Chad Tracy, posting a 5.15 ERA and 1.69 WHIP with a 1-7 record, .820 OPS allowed, and 8.9 K/9 ratio through 13 starts.

item.title: [morningjournal.com] Guardians can make it simple for clinching a 2026 postseason berth: Keep winning
item.dc:creator: Justin Lada
item.description: Baseball season’s marathon is coming down to its final sprint this week, and the Guardians are going to find out if they have enough figurative speed to finish on the podium. The Guardians did the hard work over the weekend by sweeping the Oakland/Sacramento/not-yet Las Vegas Athletics — though they had to come back on Sept. 18 and 19 — and squeaking out a 1-0 win. But style points don’t matter. Plus-one in the win column is all that counts. The Detroit Tigers begrudgingly gave Cleveland the sli
item.content:encoded:
Baseball season’s marathon is coming down to its final sprint this week, and the Guardians are going to find out if they have enough figurative speed to finish on the podium.
The Guardians did the hard work over the weekend by sweeping the Oakland/Sacramento/not-yet Las Vegas Athletics — though they had to come back on Sept. 18 and 19 — and squeaking out a 1-0 win. But style points don’t matter. Plus-one in the win column is all that counts.
The Detroit Tigers begrudgingly gave Cleveland the slightest bit of help by overcoming a six-run first inning to beat the Chicago White Sox on Sept. 18, 11-8. Unfortunately, their offense didn’t make much noise after that comeback, but it gave the Guardians just enough to climb back atop the AL Central alone.
Now, Cleveland takes its one-game lead in the AL Central and a five-game winning streak to Boston to face the freshly playoff-clinched Red Sox for three games. A series at Boston vs. the Red Sox is almost inarguably the toughest series left for Cleveland, the White Sox, and the rest of the wild card orbit of Texas, Toronto and Houston.
The White Sox will head to Kansas City this week, where the Royals are above .500 at home. Then they come back home to host the Colorado Rockies to end the regular season.
Unfortunately for the Guardians, they don’t have the safety net of any tiebreakers against teams in their orbit. A sweep of the Red Sox would give them the tiebreaker over Boston, but that wouldn’t matter as it would keep them in first place in the division going into the final weekend anyway.
The Red Sox also have their rotation lined up for the wild card Series, likely with the Yankees, since they’re close to having that locked in. Meaning Cleveland gets to face Boston’s best starting arms in Peyton Tolle, ace Sonny Gray, and another lefty in Ranger Suarez. So they all have six days of rest lined up into their starts in three-game wild card series.
Boston is six games back in the loss column of the New York Yankees, so catching them is highly improbable. Will that mean the Red Sox will get some players to rest? Possibly. They might be unlikely to push their starters too hard. But then that’s up to the Guardians’ offense to put them in that position to decide.
By virtue of holding Williams back to pitch last week in the opener vs. the White Sox, he’s not scheduled to pitch again until at least September 25 or 26. Cleveland has Parker Messick going vs. Boston in the opener, which also lines him up for regular rest on the final day of the season on Sept. 27, should Cleveland still need to win that game to get in the postseason.
The division title would be the most advantageous path for Cleveland. It would get a bye to the ALDS and host it at home, though the Guardians just did get their at-home record one game above .500 thanks to a 5-1 home stand to wrap up the regular season at Progressive Field. There is also a scenario in which Texas catches fire this week and clinches the second seed as the AL West champ and relegates Cleveland to a wild-card series no matter what. But for the Guardians, everything right now is about being one game better.
If they manage to win the division, then they can line the rotation up how they want for the ALDS.
If they are still fighting for a wild-card spot heading into the weekend in Kansas City, they would need to decide how they need to use Williams and Messick. If WIlliams starts on September 25, he could go in Game 2 of the wild card series on Sept. 30. If Messick has to pitch for the wild-card spot on Sept. 27, that takes him out of the wild-card round rotation at least on regular rest. At the very least, Cleveland needs the wild card spot wrapped up by Sept. 26, so it can skip Messick on Sept. 27, push him to Sept. 29 and have Messick and Williams lined up for Games 1 and 2.
The Guardians will either finish with another AL Central title, the franchise’s third in a row and the 14th in the history of the division, dating to its first in 1995, the last wild card spot, sending them to the worst division winner, possibly Houston or Texas, and then onto the White Sox IF they get past the wild card round. That means this final road trip could be a four-city, two-week tour to play the most meaningful and stressful baseball all year.
Or: They could miss the playoffs entirely. Thinking about some of those losses earlier in the year at St. Louis and Juan Brito’s error and one of the few Cade Smith blown saves. Or another one of his blown saves during the sweep by the Mets with two outs at home after the trade deadline.
Without having any tiebreakers over teams competing for playoff spots with them, the Guardians have to be one game better than any of them for a playoff spot. Be it the division or the wild card. That means winning one game at a time and just needing to be one run and one game better.

item.title: [bostonglobe.com] Red Sox offense has been running on fumes down the stretch - The Boston Globe

Wilyer Abreu (7 for 36), Mickey Gasper (4 for 25), Jahmai Jones (2 for 18), Isiah Kiner-Falefa (1 for 20), Adley Rutschman (6 for 30), and Nick Sogard (8 for 40) have all gone cold. item.content:encoded:
Call it a product of injuries or just a slump, but the Red Sox are staggering into the final week of the regular season offensively.
They have averaged 2.82 runs over the last 11 games, hitting .210 with a .621 OPS.
Wilyer Abreu (7 for 36), Mickey Gasper (4 for 25), Jahmai Jones (2 for 18), Isiah Kiner-Falefa (1 for 20), Adley Rutschman (6 for 30), and Nick Sogard (8 for 40) have all gone cold.
Roman Anthony was 5 for 13 with two doubles and a home run over the weekend against the Rays after hitting .137 in his 12 prior games.
The Sox are eighth in the American League in runs scored (678, 4.35 per game). They were third last season at 4.85.
“Just got to stay with it,” interim manager Chad Tracy said after a 5-1 loss against the Rays on Sunday. “Obviously we’ve got to hit and score runs. But we’re getting our way back to health, and we’ll get there.”
The return of two of the team’s top hitters, Willson Contreras and Ceddanne Rafaela, should help.
Contreras has played only four games this month because of a strained left hamstring and a bruised right hand. He started swinging a bat Sunday and hopes to return this week after missing the Rays series.
“It’s getting better every day,” Contreras said Sunday. “We’ll see.”
Contreras leads the team in home runs (27), RBIs (81), and OPS (.905).
Rafaela should be back in the lineup Tuesday after missing 16 games with a right quadriceps strain. He has hit .282 with a .760 OPS, 16 homers, and 70 RBIs.
Caleb Durbin has reached base in 13 consecutive games, raising his on-base percentage from .324 to .338.
Trevor Story has been another positive, hitting .338 with an .869 OPS and 10 RBIs over 19 games since returning from the injured list.
Tests this week
The postseason doesn’t start until Sept. 29, but the Red Sox will get a taste of what’s to come this week at Fenway Park.
They start a three-game series against the Guardians on Tuesday before the Cubs arrive Friday.
The 81-75 Guardians hold a one-game lead over the White Sox in the American League Central. The 87-69 Cubs are tied with the Padres atop the National League wild-card race.
The Guardians have All-Star lefthander Parker Messick (12-9, 2.57) starting Tuesday with Foster Griffin (15-5, 3.67) on Wednesday. Messick faced the Sox in Cleveland on May 30 and allowed one run over five innings.
The Sox have Payton Tolle, Sonny Gray, and Ranger Suarez lined up in the series, which could be how they approach the Wild Card Series next week.
Honor for Arias
Shortstop Franklin Arias was named the Eastern League’s Most Valuable Player and Top Prospect by Minor League Baseball. The 20-year-old from Venezuela hit .318 with a .993 OPS in 75 games for Portland before he was promoted to Triple-A Worcester. Sea Dogs first baseman Brooks Bannon also was named to the Eastern All-Star team. The Pitcher of the Year was righthander Anthony Eyanson, who was 4-0 with a 1.69 ERA in 11 games for Portland before going to the Orioles organization in the trade for Rutschman . . . The Sox finished 46-35 on the road, a five-game improvement on last season . . . Assistant general managers Mike Groopman and Taylor Smith interviewed with the Athletics, who are searching for a head of baseball operations after firing David Forst in August. Longtime assistant GM Billy Owens also is a candidate, along with former Nationals GM Mike Rizzo and former Astros GM James Click, who now works for the Blue Jays.
Peter Abraham can be reached at peter.abraham@globe.com. Follow him on Bluesky at peteabeglobe.bsky.social.

item.title: [BoSox Injection] Red Sox may not reunite with Alex Bregman for final Cubs series following unlucky injury
item.dc:creator: Katie Manganelli
item.description: Shortly after the Boston Red Sox lost out on Alex Bregman in free agency, fans looked to find the reunion between the two sides. The Chicago Cubs will be in town for the final series of the season from September 25-27, but the reunion with Bregman will probably look much different than fans expected days ago. item.content:encoded:
Shortly after the Boston Red Sox lost out on Alex Bregman in free agency, fans looked to find the reunion between the two sides. The Chicago Cubs will be in town for the final series of the season from September 25-27, but the reunion with Bregman will probably look much different than fans expected days ago.
On September 20, while he was standing near the on-deck circle warming up for his next at-bat, Bregman was hit in the face with a foul ball. The ball shot off Michael Busch's bat on a line and hit the third baseman square in the cheek. It happened so fast there was no chance of dodging it. He immediately buried his face in his hands and descended the dugout steps with a trainer.
After the game, Bregman shared a picture of his face (don't click if you're squeamish), featuring a swollen-shut black eye and a bloodied cheek. He posted another picture the following morning and the entire left half of his face was swollen.
The Cubs sent Bregman to the hospital after the injury. According to Chicago manager Craig Counsell said Bregman was hit in the left cheekbone just under his eye and his nose was bleeding after the hit. Jeff Passan on September 21 reported that Bregman has multiple facial fractures and that he will not undergo surgery — although that doesn't exactly mean he doesn't need it. Passan says Bregman hopes to return during the postseason, but he might be too banged up to pull it off.
Alex Bregman not likley to play in Cubs series against Red Sox following unlucky hit by foul ball near the on-deck circle
While there's still no diagnosis, it's hard to forsee Bregman returning from this injury in a timely manner. Not only will he most likely miss his series at Fenway Park, but he could be out for Chicago's playoff run, depending how far it goes.
Bregman got off to a slow start with the Cubs this season but got rolling at the plate in the second half. He batted .241/.336/.359 over 45 games before the All-Star break and .296/.378/.600 through 44 games after the Midsummer Classic. Bregman has hit 17 home runs in the second half, nearly doubling his nine-homer total from the first half.
Besides National League MVP candidate Pete Crow-Armstrong, Bregman has been the Cubs' biggest offensive contributor in the second half. He would've been key to their playoff push and his absence will be rough for the lineup.
The National League Wild Card race is neck-and-neck as Bregman lands out of commission. The Cubs and San Diego Padres are currently tied for the first Wild Card spot with the Philadelphia Phillies trailing one game behind. Bregman won't be able to help his team fight for the best possible standing and they could end up facing a dangerous team in the first round, such as the Los Angeles Dodgers or Milwaukee Brewers.
Bregman also won't be able to stick it to the Red Sox, the team that traded its franchise third baseman to accommodate him, then didn't beat the best offer for his services in free agency. It's probably better for Boston that he doesn't have the chance to hit at Fenway Park again so soon.

item.title: [bleedcubbieblue.com] Who plays third base if Alex Bregman has to miss time?
item.dc:creator: Sara Sanchez
item.description: It was a very scary moment during Sunday’s game against the Reds when Michael Busch hit a foul ball that Alex Bregman was unable to avoid as he warmed up on deck. Al already summarized what we know from the injury (and there likely won’t be another update until tomorrow due to today’s off day), but an uneasy question remains. With six games remaining in the regular season and the Cubs one game from clinching a berth in the Wild Card round, today we need to take a closer look at what the Cubs off
item.content:encoded:
It was a very scary moment during Sunday’s game against the Reds when Michael Busch hit a foul ball that Alex Bregman was unable to avoid as he warmed up on deck. Al already summarized what we know from the injury (and there likely won’t be another update until tomorrow due to today’s off day), but an uneasy question remains.
With six games remaining in the regular season and the Cubs one game from clinching a berth in the Wild Card round, today we need to take a closer look at what the Cubs offense and defense might look like if they are without their star third baseman for any length of time.
Even writing that sucks, a lot. After some early season struggles at the plate, Bregman is currently the second best hitter on the Cubs and it’s not particularly close. As I detailed less than a week ago, he’s been the second best hitter in all of baseball since the All Star Game, behind likely National League MVP, Pete Crow-Armstrong. Those numbers have shifted slightly since last week, with Fernando Tatis Jr. inching ahead of Bregman via fWAR in the last few games, but it’s still a potentially huge loss for any team.
It may be an even bigger loss for the 2026 Cubs than it would be for other teams in the Postseason hunt. The Cubs competitive edge is built almost entirely on elite offense and defense. You can see how the Cubs rank in a number of categories below:
Cubs 2026 MLB ranks by category
| Category | Rank |
|---|---|
| Offense | 1st |
| Defense | 1st |
| Pitching | 29th |
| Starting Pitching | 26th |
| Relief Pitching | 28th |
It’s old news at this point, but the reason the Cubs are where they are in the standings is their bats and their gloves. The pitching has been questionable at the best moments and that success is built on the ability of the Cubs defenders to turn weak contact into outs while outscoring their opponents. The former is what allows them to win games where they are giving up way more runs than they should.
Bregman isn’t just a team leader. He isn’t merely the big free agent signing who has set the tone for the Cubs. He’s their second-best hitter since the All-Star break, and their third best hitter during the 2026 season (behind Seiya Suzuki). He’s their fourth best defender this season (behind PCA, Dansby Swanson and Nico Hoerner). So let’s just stipulate up front that if the Cubs need to replace Bregman it will be very difficult, if not impossible, to replicate that production. Below are select stats for all of the Cubs who have at least 180 plate appearances in 2026:
2026 Cubs Select Stats
| Name | G | PA | HR | R | RBI | SB | BB% | K% | ISO | BABIP | AVG | OBP | SLG | wOBA | xwOBA | wRC+ | BsR | Off | Def | WAR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pete Crow-Armstrong | 156 | 702 | 45 | 118 | 107 | 38 | 11.11% | 25.93% | .298 | .326 | .280 | .371 | .578 | .402 | .377 | 157 | 7.3 | 55.9 | 23.8 | 10.4 |

The most obvious solution is a combination of Pedro Ramírez and Matt Shaw filling in at third base. In limited sample sizes, Ramírez has hit .350/.409/.575 with a wRC+ of 172 in 44 plate appearances against left-handed pitching. Shaw has hit .273/.367/.468 with a wRC+ of 132 against lefties. The results have not been as good against righties for either hitter. Ramírez is slashing .247/.305/.385 with a wRC+ of 89 in 201 plate appearances against righties while Shaw is slashing .205/.295/.373 with a wRC+ of 86 in 97 plate appearances against righties.
Neither is in the same category of defender as Bregman, who should compete for his second Gold Glove this season. You can see the OAA leaderboard from Statcast below:
It’s definitely not ideal, but winning baseball seasons always have a curveball or two. Here’s hoping the Cubs receive good news on Bregman after more tests are run and he’s able to rejoin the team quickly. In the meantime, it’s quite the opportunity for a couple of the Cubs young infielders to make their mark on a Cubs Postseason run. If he can’t play himself, I imagine no one will be cheering for Pedro and Shaw more than Bregman.

item.title: [tsn.ca] The latest on MLB postseason clinches, Ohtani and Judge health updates, awards races and more
item.dc:creator: The Associated Press
item.description: Major League Baseball's postseason is rapidly approaching, with the Los Angeles Dodgers seeking a third straight World Series title. It remains to be seen how much some of the game's biggest stars will be able to participate in the playoffs, though. The Dodgers are once again among the best teams in the big leagues, and they'll have several challengers in October, including the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays. All three teams could finish the regular season with 100 wins or more. Los Angele
item.content:encoded:
Major League Baseball's postseason is rapidly approaching, with the Los Angeles Dodgers seeking a third straight World Series title. It remains to be seen how much some of the game's biggest stars will be able to participate in the playoffs, though.
The Dodgers are once again among the best teams in the big leagues, and they'll have several challengers in October, including the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays. All three teams could finish the regular season with 100 wins or more. Los Angeles is rolling even though four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani’s health is a concern.
The New York Yankees, Boston Red Sox and Atlanta Braves have also clinched spots in the postseason. Yankees slugger Aaron Judge, a three-time AL MVP, is dealing with a right calf strain that will keep him on the injured list until at least the final day of the regular season this Sunday.
While the 12-team playoff field appears mostly set, there are a few long-shot contenders for the postseason, and specific matchups are in flux.
Here's some of what to watch as the season comes to a close.
Here's who can clinch a playoff spot Monday
No team can clinch a playoff spot on Monday, with most of the league getting a day off.
There was one important game in the American League, where the Toronto Blue Jays lost 4-3 in Baltimore to the Orioles. The Blue Jays fell 3 1/2 games behind the Chicago White Sox for the final AL wild card. Baltimore is 4 1/2 games behind. Both the Blue Jays and Orioles can be eliminated as soon as Tuesday.
AL race is murky while NL is more defined
There's quite a bit of mediocrity in the AL Central and West divisions this season, which has led to some fascinating pennant races and could lead to a sub-.500 team making the postseason.
The Cleveland Guardians (81-75) have a narrow advantage over the Chicago White Sox (80-76) in the AL Central while the Texas Rangers (78-78) are just ahead of the Houston Astros (77-79) in the AL West.
Over in the National League, the playoff bracket is close to set.
The Chicago Cubs (87-69), San Diego Padres (87-69) and Philadelphia Phillies (86-70) are jockeying for position in the wild-card race but will almost certainly make the postseason. The only team within shouting distance is the Arizona Diamondbacks (82-74), who are four games back.
MVP races, stats to watch
MLB's major awards probably won't have much drama this season.
Both MVP races have strong favorites with Chicago's Pete Crow-Armstrong running away with the NL honor while Houston's Yordan Alvarez is the probable choice in the AL, though Tampa Bay's Junior Caminero has also had a fantastic season. Alvarez still has a shot at a rare Triple Crown. He leads the AL in batting average at .313 but his 40 homers are one behind Caminero and his 99 RBIs are nine back of Baltimore's Pete Alonso.
For the Cy Young Award, Milwaukee flame thrower Jacob Misiorowski and New York ace Cam Schlittler are the favorites in the NL and AL, respectively.
The Rookie of the Year races also look set with Cincinnati's Sal Stewart and his 110-RBI season the leader in the NL and Detroit's Kevin McGonigle the favorite in the AL.
What is the MLB playoff format?
There are 12 teams that qualify for MLB’s postseason, including six teams from both the AL and NL. The three division winners in each league get seeds No. 1 through No. 3, ranked by win-loss record. Then the three wild-card teams get seeds No. 4 through No. 6, also ranked by win-loss record.
The top two teams with the best record in both the AL and NL automatically advance to the Division Series. The other eight teams play in the Wild Card Series, which is a best-of-three format beginning on Tuesday, Sept. 30. In both the AL and NL, the No. 6 seed will travel to face the No. 3 seed while the No. 5 seed goes to No. 4. The higher seed hosts all three games.
The winners then advance to the best-of-five Division Series, followed by the best-of-seven League Championship Series and a best-of-seven World Series between the winners of the AL and NL.
What is the MLB postseason schedule?
Wild Card Round: Sept. 29-Oct. 1 (NBC/Peacock)
Division Series: Oct. 3-10 (AL on TBS, NL on FOX/FS1)
Championship Series: Oct. 11-20 (AL on TBS, NL on FOX/FS1)
World Series: Oct. 23-31 (FOX)
Who are the favorites to win the World Series?
The Dodgers (+220) are the favorites to capture a third straight World Series title while the Brewers (+600), Yankees (+800) and Rays (+800) are viewed as the top contenders.
___
See AP’s full MLB coverage here
David Brandt, The Associated Press

item.title: [Talk Sox] Adley Rutschman's September Bounce Back Continues His Offensive Rollercoaster
item.dc:creator: Sam Stargell
item.description: Red Sox Video Boston Red Sox catcher Adley Rutschman had a hot start to the month of September, hitting three home runs in four games. Since then, Rutschman's batting average has tumbled, though he's maintained an excellent .500 slugging percentage. His September output presents another shift in what has been an up and down year offensively. To paint the picture, a good starting place would be to look at his wRC+ in each month of the season. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | As you can s
item.content:encoded:
Red Sox Video
Boston Red Sox catcher Adley Rutschman had a hot start to the month of September, hitting three home runs in four games. Since then, Rutschman's batting average has tumbled, though he's maintained an excellent .500 slugging percentage.
His September output presents another shift in what has been an up and down year offensively. To paint the picture, a good starting place would be to look at his wRC+ in each month of the season.
| | | | | | |
| | | | | | |
As you can see, his season has not been consistent. Two caveats to point out here are the obvious trade from Baltimore to Boston, and his extensive time on the injured list. Anytime you have those factors at play, it has the chance to lead to inconsistency.
Still, in August, Rutschman had a slash line of .170/.254/.245 to go with an OPS of .500. Now in September, he has a .217/.250/.500 slash line and a .750 OPS. You can see that his average, slugging percentage, and OPS have increased sharply despite a drop in his on-base percentage.
Now, of course, you will expect some fluctuation from month to month throughout the course of the season. But what has led to this latest shift in the star backstop's performance at the plate?
Well, you've got a significant decline in walk rate (10.2% to 4.5%), which is owed to the fact that his swing rate has exploded (from 35.6% to 40.1%). He's simply taken on a more aggressive approach at the plate, which has created some fascinating discrepancies in his numbers.
Against fastballs he has a .318 average and a .727 SLG while averaging a 94 mph exit velocity on balls in play. Against breaking balls, however, he has a .200 average and a .600 SLG with his exit velocity ticking down to 83.5 MPH. The statistics plummet even further against off-speed pitches, to the point where he has essentially produced nothing against them in September.
When you get a hold of fastballs it can lead to extra bases, which it has in this case. When you can't produce well against an entire repertoire of pitches you will continue to see a lower batting average, low walk rate, and lower on-base percentage. There is also some luck leading to this output; his expected batting average and slugging percentage against fastballs this month are less impressive (.255 xBA and a .560 xSLG) that the actual results.
Essentially, even what he has been doing well is a little inflated.
All in all, Adley Rutschman has been better in September than any time since he arrived in Boston. That is a good sign, as the Red Sox will need him in the playoffs. But temper expectations for an October breakout—the underlying statistics are not indicative of a hitter who has fully found his stride at the plate.

item.title: [concordmonitor.com] 'What does this all mean?': Rundlett Middle School displays artifacts from unearthed time capsules - Concord Monitor
item.dc:creator: Yasmeen Saadi

item.content:encoded:
A Red Sox vs. Yankees ticket stub from May 31, 1976, was Concord Historical Society volunteer Bill Kretovic’s favorite item from a time capsule buried at Rundlett Middle School.
The game took place just 11 days after the famous bench-clearing brawl between the Red Sox and Yankees when Boston catcher Carlton Fisk tagged out Yankee outfielder Lou Piniella. Tensions were still high as angry Red Sox fans threw debris and exploded firecrackers at the Yankees players.
The red, white and blue stub, partially ripped on the bottom, still displays the date and price of the game — $5. Kretovic found an old retainer buried alongside the ticket. While less historically significant, it still intrigued him.
“I think of that as like someone coming home from school that day and going, ‘I lost my retainer, Mom!’ And it’s actually in the time capsule,” Kretovic said.
Dozens of artifacts, including the ticket and the retainer, sprawled across tables inside a basement storage area in Rundlett Middle School. The items were found in two containers buried in the middle school’s courtyard back when it was a junior high school. On Sept. 11, Kretovic dug up the time capsules and has since been drying and researching the items inside.
“Throughout this process, it’s kind of funny, because I really kind of have a little bit of like, ‘Am I Indiana Jones? Am I Marty McFly in ‘Back to the Future?'” Kretovic said. “I come down here, and that stuff is 30 years old; this stuff is 50 years old. Then, I go back upstairs, and it’s 2026.”
Alumni get a first look
On Friday, the Concord High School Class of 1976 gathered for its 50-year reunion. As part of their tour, alumni got the first look at the newly recovered artifacts.
“While this stuff is technically not theirs, they may have information as to where maybe their time capsule is,” Kretovic said. “But it’s from their era. And I think they can see and they can go, ‘Okay, yep, saddle shoes, we all wore those.'”
In addition to the 1976 artifacts, visiting alumni got to see items from the time capsule buried in 1992 by the class of 1995. The four trash bins that made up the capsule were uncovered in June.
The 1992 capsule contained VCRs, a cassette tape, Nintendo games, Rolling Stone magazines, a class schedule and pop culture items.
Cathy Dawson and her husband, Michael Painter, came up from Florida to join the reunion.
“It’s amazing and fun, I mean, just to think, ‘Wow, 50 years ago, they buried it,'” Painter said.
His wife completed his thought: “And just remembering it now and to have it on our 50th high school reunion, too, it really just makes it special,” she said.
Painter said the tour reminded him of how simple life was back then.
“I’ll be looking forward to what they got 50 years from now,” Painter said.
Finding the 1976 time capsule
Nathan Amsden carefully drew a map to his class time capsule in June 1976. Next to an arrow pointing to the time capsule, Amsden wrote, “To be opened in June, 2004.”
Kretovic used this map, the Pythagorean Theorem and his tape measure to find the marked spot and dig over the course of two days.
“We weren’t really sure what material it was made out of,” Kretovic said. “So, if it was metal, it could have been rusted away. If it was wood, it could have been rotted away. Just had no idea.”
As he dug, Kretovic maneuvered around some metal plates and the large root of a nearby tree, planted after the time capsule was buried.
“As I was doing that, I was about ready to call it quits, because I said, ‘I’m down this far, I don’t know if it’s gone, if someone already found it'” Kretovic said. “So, as I’m digging some of the dirt out and tossing it up onto the piles over here, I notice that piece of plastic.”
That plastic was the top of two hard plastic barrels: the 1976 time capsules.
After finding the containers, Kretovic walked middle school students through the process of how he found the spot using the map.
“We asked them how old their parents were, and one girl said, ‘Oh, 39!’ I’m like, okay, how old are your grandparents?” Kretovic said.
Having located, unearthed, restored and researched many of the artifacts, Kretovic asked himself, ‘What does this all mean?’
“There was some thought going into what we’re putting in here for people to see, in this case, 30 years from now,” Kretovic said, pointing to some of the items buried in 1992. “What we had on our minds and what was going on.”
The 1976 and 1992 time capsules are not alone.
One buried in 1989 by the class of 1992 has been located, but is paved over and will be dug up later. Another, created in 1988 by the class of 1991 was never buried and is not yet opened.
The hunt for time capsules started when Rundlett librarian Regina Wall told Principal Jay Richard she wanted to create another time capsule to mark the new building. Richard then remembered a box he found when he arrived at Rundlett. It contained envelopes with hand-drawn maps from students showing where their time capsule was buried.
Since then, Richard has contacted alumni and sought the help of the historical society to find and uncover past time capsules as construction continues for the new middle school.
As the middle school considers creating another time capsule, Kretovic recommends an above-ground model.
When he opened up the 1992 bins, Kretovic discovered each bin had three plastic liners with items put in multiple bags and sealed inside Ziplocs as well.
Despite that effort, Kretovic said some of the bags were like fishbowls that he had to pop and drain out. Many of the items sustained water damage. To ensure items are preserved going forward, he suggested a room inside the new school with drawers to store artifacts for each year.
As of now, Kretovic said he is not sure what will happen to the items recovered from the time capsules, but he plans to support Richard with what he and the school choose to do.

item.title: [yanksgoyard.com] Red Sox-Cubs weather nightmare could give Yankees a surprising playoff edge
item.dc:creator: Adam Weinrib
item.description: Fans of the Boston Red Sox are about to become bigger fans of the Philadelphia Phillies and San Diego Padres than they've ever been. And fans of the New York Yankees are about to get a renewed interest in destructive weather systems. With Boston and New York all but fated to meet next week in a best-of-three Wild Card Series, the Yankees are suddenly invested in a chaotic super storm that might interfere with the Sox's meaningful weekend series with the Chicago Cubs. If the Cubs' playoff positio
item.content:encoded:
Fans of the Boston Red Sox are about to become bigger fans of the Philadelphia Phillies and San Diego Padres than they've ever been. And fans of the New York Yankees are about to get a renewed interest in destructive weather systems.
With Boston and New York all but fated to meet next week in a best-of-three Wild Card Series, the Yankees are suddenly invested in a chaotic super storm that might interfere with the Sox's meaningful weekend series with the Chicago Cubs. If the Cubs' playoff positioning is at stake - right now, they're tied atop the Wild Card standings with the Padres and one game ahead of the Phillies - these games will need to be completed, whether or not they have any significance to the Sox. Bostonians probably hope the Cubs slip up before they ever arrive at Fenway while the Pads and Phils surge.
It seems very likely these games will need to be completed, though. It also seems very likely these games will be washed out, leading to either a baseball game (or two!) taking up Boston's lone off day before the start of the postseason, or an emergency roadtrip to Chicago disrupting things in a different way.
Will Red Sox insane weather weekend against Cubs hurt their chances against Yankees in playoffs?
Now, counterpoint, we know how much the Red Sox tend to excel when faced with plane trauma or travel trouble of any kind. Does extreme weather also make them superhuman? I, for one, do not want to find out.
Objectively, though, even if they rest all their starters and even if they have zero members of the playoff rotation penciled into this Cubs series, all lined up for the previous showdown with the Cleveland Guardians ... this has to have an effect, doesn't it? It's in MLB's absolute best interest to avoid any nonsense here. Cram a doubleheader into Friday. Tell John Henry he's about to lose some gate receipts and push this whole series to Chicago. The impact on the Wild Card Series is too great.
And you thought this weekend of baseball was meaningless, didn't you, Yankees fans? Joke's on you.
Payton Tolle, Sonny Gray, and Ranger Suárez will all be out of commission either way, but any undue duress that removes a clean reset point from the Sox while allowing the Yankees to veg out and get in the right mindset can certainly swing things a bit. And if this series is crucial to the Cubs, MLB won't love Boston trying to rest their starters and back away from the competition either. This is about to be fascinating, strange, and a potentially damaging wrinkle in any playoff preview.

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

21 Sep 2026, 22:49 GMT+10

(Photo credit: David Dermer)
The Cleveland Guardians are playing some of their best baseball of the season at the most important time, and they will attempt to extend a five-game winning streak when they visit the Boston Red Sox on Tuesday.
Cleveland (81-75) has a one-game lead over the Chicago White Sox for first place in the American League Central standings with six games remaining. After playing three games at Boston, the Guardians will wrap up the regular season with a three-game road series against the Kansas City Royals.
The Guardians also have a three-game lead over the Texas Rangers, who are at the top of the American League West standings. Cleveland and Texas are among the teams battling for the AL's No. 2 seed, which comes with a first-round bye.
'The feeling in the clubhouse is pretty awesome right now,' Cleveland closer Cade Smith said after he earned his 39th save in 44 opportunities when the Guardians beat the Athletics 1-0 Sunday. 'We've got some momentum. We've got confidence in the way we're playing. We're playing clean baseball.
'There's this kind of calm focus that we're ready to go out there and play. We're looking forward to taking it one game at a time and finishing strong and setting us up for the postseason.'
The Guardians went 10-20 in their first 30 games after the All-Star break and were a season-high five games under .500 (61-66) at that point but have gone 20-9 since then.
'One day at a time,' Cleveland manager Stephen Vogt said. 'We can only control today. Let's go 1-0 every day and let's worry about tomorrow, tomorrow, because here we are, one week to go, six games to go. We're right in it and we have a great opportunity in front of us.'
Despite dropping a 5-1 decision to the Tampa Bay Rays on Sunday, Boston (84-72) clinched a playoff spot when the Houston Astros lost to the Atlanta Braves. A postseason berth didn't seem likely when the Red Sox had a 32-46 record on June 24.
'They didn't take no for an answer,' said interim manager Chad Tracy, who took over a 10-17 team when he replaced Alex Cora on April 26. 'When you work as hard as we have worked, it was almost July (before we got going), and to fight as hard as we did, to put ourselves in the position we did, I don't think you care much how (the spot is clinched). You just want to see your ticket get punched.'
The Red Sox will almost certainly open the playoffs with a best-of-three wild-card series on the road against the New York Yankees. Boston and New York also met in the wild-card round last year, when the Yankees won the series in three games.
Boston also has six regular-season games remaining. After the three-game series against the Guardians, Boston will play three home games against the Chicago Cubs.
Tuesday's pitching matchup features a pair of left-handers in Cleveland's Parker Messick (12-9, 2.57 ERA) and Boston's Payton Tolle (9-6, 3.02). Tolle was originally scheduled to pitch over the weekend against Tampa Bay, but had his start pushed back as Boston lines up its pitching for the postseason.
Messick doesn't have a decision against Boston but has a 4.15 ERA in two career appearances (both starts). Tolle has not pitched against Cleveland during his career.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [CBS Sports] Alex Bregman 'hopeful' to be available for Cubs in playoffs after getting hit in face by foul ball, per report
item.dc:creator: Mike Axisa
item.description: Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman suffered multiple facial fractures on the left side when he was struck by a foul ball while in the on-deck circle during Sunday's game, reports ESPN. He will not have surgery and is hopeful to return for the postseason. "It's just an unfortunate accident. I'm hoping and praying he is all right," manager Craig Counsell said after the game (via MLB.com). "We have to get good results from the hospital first. He got hit in the face, so you are worried about hi
item.content:encoded:
Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman suffered multiple facial fractures on the left side when he was struck by a foul ball while in the on-deck circle during Sunday's game, reports ESPN. He will not have surgery and is hopeful to return for the postseason.
"It's just an unfortunate accident. I'm hoping and praying he is all right," manager Craig Counsell said after the game (via MLB.com). "We have to get good results from the hospital first. He got hit in the face, so you are worried about his general well-being first. If we get a good report, we'll move to the next step. I want to get a good report."
The fluke injury occurred when Michael Busch hit a check swing foul ball Bregman's way in the fourth inning. Bregman simply did not have enough time to react given his proximity to home plate. He shared an update on social media Monday morning:
Alex Bregman shared another update to his IG story this morning of how his face is looking after getting hit with the foul ball yesterday:
[image or embed]
Other than pain tolerance, the biggest question is whether the swelling will subside soon enough so that Bregman can see out of his left eye. If his vision is impaired, he won't be able to play. There's pretty much no way around that.
Only seven days remain in the regular season. If the Cubs place Bregman on the 10-day injured list, he would not be eligible to play in the Wild Card Series next week, but would be able to return for the NLDS, should the Cubs advance. Chicago is five games up on a wild-card spot and can clinch a postseason berth as early as Tuesday with a win over the Marlins or a loss by the Diamondbacks. They have been eliminated from the NL Central race.
As things stand headed into Monday's slate, the Cubs are lined up to face the Padres, though the NL wild-card race seeding is still up in the air.
If Bregman is unable to play in the Wild Card Series, some combination of Matt Shaw and Pedro Ramírez would likely fill in, though that certainly would be a downgrade. Instead, the Cubs would have to rely more heavily on National League MVP frontrunner Pete Crow-Armstrong, Seiya Suzuki, Dansby Swanson, Nico Hoerner and others.
Bregman, 32, is hitting .262/.352/.452 with 26 home runs this season. He has 19 homers in his last 61 games and has been Chicago's second-best player behind Crow-Armstrong. This is the first year of Bregman's five-year, $175 million contract with the Cubs.

item.title: [Sportsnet.ca] Report: Cubs' Bregman won't need surgery for facial fracture
item.dc:creator: Sportsnet Staff
item.description: Alex Bregman has avoided the worst-case scenario after a scary incident on Sunday. The Chicago Cubs star third baseman suffered multiple facial fractures after being struck by a foul ball while standing in the on-deck circle, but will not undergo surgery and is hopeful to return in the post-season, ESPN's Jeff Passan reported on Monday. In the fourth inning, left-handed batting Michael Busch checked his swing and fouled off a pitch from Reds right-hander Luis Mey that struck Bregman, who immedia
item.content:encoded:
Alex Bregman has avoided the worst-case scenario after a scary incident on Sunday.
The Chicago Cubs star third baseman suffered multiple facial fractures after being struck by a foul ball while standing in the on-deck circle, but will not undergo surgery and is hopeful to return in the post-season, ESPN's Jeff Passan reported on Monday.
In the fourth inning, left-handed batting Michael Busch checked his swing and fouled off a pitch from Reds right-hander Luis Mey that struck Bregman, who immediately jogged toward the Cubs' dugout with his hand covering the left side of his face.
Bregman was escorted by a trainer down the dugout steps and into the clubhouse, with blood visible on his face. Matt Shaw replaced Bregman and drew a walk. He remained in the game to play second base, with Pedro Ramirez shifting to third.
“It just happens so fast,” Busch said. “(Mey)'s throwing the ball hard and it comes off hard. Any time it enters the head area, it's always a scary thing. We try to focus on the game, but it's tough. Hopefully he's OK, first and foremost.”
Bregman has contributed 26 home runs to a Cubs offence that leads MLB with 217 round-trippers. The 32-year-old also has .262/.352/.452 slash line and 89 RBIs.
The Cubs can clinch a playoff spot with either a win or an Arizona Diamondbacks loss on Tuesday.
—With files from The Associated Press

After a promising start to the season (remember when the Rockies went 13-14 in April?), the Rockies are one loss away from their fifth straight 100-plus-loss season. That’s largely due to a 7-25 skid since Aug. 17.
With Colorado (57-99) hosting the Arizona Diamondbacks (82-74) in its home finale Tuesday through Thursday, it’s hard to tune in with much optimism or interest right now. However, whether you plan on going to 20th and Blake to catch one last game or you’ll be tuning into Rockies.TV or KOA radio, here are some individual milestones and bright spots to look for in the final action at Coors Field in 2026.
Bark at the Park
With temperatures projected to be in the low 80s and high 70s, it’s a perfect time to bring out the dogs to Coors Field! Both Tuesday’s and Wednesday’s games will feature canines of all shapes and sizes participating in the pre-game parade for the annual Bark at the Park games. Regardless of what’s happening on the field, it’s aways fun to see the Simba Cam and how Ryan Spilborghs will interact with the dogs and fans in the stands.
K-Free’s final start as a Rockie at Coors?
131 Games over 10 seasons.
687 innings pitched.
Through the ups and downs, Kyle Freeland has been there for the Rockies. In those 131 games at Coors Field, which include 128 starts, Freeland has gone 40-40 with a 4.97 ERA and 538 strikeouts.
When he takes the mound on Tuesday against the Diamondbacks, it’s possible that it could be his last start as a Rockie at Coors Field. While Freeland, 33, has certainly had his share of struggles this year and in his career, this season he’s recorded four quality starts, including the first complete game in his career — an 8-1 win over Kansas City in the Mile High City on Aug. 2.
This season marks the end of Freeland’s five-year, $64.5 million deal. His future is unknown, and he could certainly be re-signed to stay with his hometown team. The majority of the Purple Row community believes that will be the case. Either way, it’s worth noting the history that might happen on Tuesday.
McCarthy’s triples and on-base streak
One of the most fun and exciting additions to the 2026 Rockies has been Jake McCarthy. Not only has he stepped up to be a great leadoff hitter, but his speed and ability to come up with clutch hits have made the Rockies a bigger threat at the plate.
The first thing to watch with McCarthy is to see if he can continue his on-base streak through the final homestand. McCarthy has currently reached base 22 games in a row, which is a career high for the former Diamondback. What a way to show the team that traded him what they are missing by stretching that to 25 games?
McCarthy hit a triple on Sunday against Seattle to extend his 22-game streak.
The 13th three-bagger of the year is currently the second-most in MLB behind Arizona’s Corbin Carroll, who has 16. McCarthy’s 13 triples are one shy of tying Charlie Blackmon (2017) for the second-most in a single season and only two behind Dexter Fowler’s single-season franchise best 15 in 2010. Nine of McCarthy’s triples have come at home this season. In an even deeper dive, McCarthy’s six triples during his 22-game on-base streak make him the third Rockie with six or more triples in a 22-game span in franchise history, joining Fowler (2011 and 2012) and Juan Uribe (2001).
The final thing to watch is McCarthy’s batting average. Entering the Arizona series, McCarthy is batting .297, which ranks No. 8 in MLB and No. 6 in the National League. Maybe McCarthy can take advantage of the spacious outfield at Coors Field by adding a triple or two and increasing his batting average.
Rumfield’s 24-game streak, AVG and OBP
Perhaps it’s fitting that during the same season that Todd Helton’s statue was unveiled at 20th and Blake, the Rockies seem to have found their first baseman of the future. Rumfield has proved to be the hitter the Rockies needed as a tough out who always finds a way to get on base.
Rumfield drew his 71st walk of the season to extend his on-base streak to 24 games on Sunday. On Saturday, Rumfield went 2-for-4 with an RBI and one run scored to help the Rockies beat Seattle 5-3.
Rumfield’s 24 games is the longest active streak in the Majors. It is also the longest on-base streak by a Rockie since Tyler Freeman’s 25-game streak, June 13-July 12, 2025.
Going into Tuesday, Rumfield is batting .300./.392/.451 with 71 walks and 85 strikeouts. His batting average is No. 7 in MLB and No. 5 in the National League, while his OBP is third-best in MLB and second in the National League behind Milwaukee’s Jake Bauers (.397). His numbers put him into tiers with veteran All-Stars like Jordan Alvarez and Luis Arraez, which is all the more impressive considering he’s a rookie. If he can finish hitting above .300, it will be the first time for a Rockie since Nolan Arenado (.315) and Trevor Story (.314) did it in 2019.
Then take McCarthy and Rumfield together. They are the first pair of Rockies to have an active on-base streak of at least 20 games at the same time since Charlie Blackmon (22g) and Elehuris Montero (26g) in 2023.
Goodman reaching the 40-HR milestone
Last season, Goodman had an outstanding year with 31 homers, 91 RBIs and hitting .278/.323/.520 in his first All-Star campaign. This season, he returned to the All-Star Game and enters the final homestand hitting .245/.312/.528 with 39 homers and 82 RBIs.
It would be so fitting for Goodman to hit his 40th home run at Coors Field to close out 2026. If he can hit the 40-HR milestone, whether it’s at home or in the final series of 2026 at the Chicago White Sox, Goodman will become the first Rockie to hit 40 homers since Arenado hit 41 in 2019.
It might be a long shot for Goodman to hit his 40th at Coors Field since only 16 of his 39 have come at home. But anything could happen, especially considering No. 39 came on Sunday vs. the Mariners, even though it was his first Coors Field homer since Aug. 1 vs. Kansas City.
Final thoughts
Despite the Rockies going out with a whimper instead of a bang, the end of a season can be a bittersweet feeling as it’s never fun when baseball is over. With 100 losses seeming unavoidable, at least there are some smaller, individual things to watch for.
What are you excited about in the final three games at Coors this season? Anything you’re hoping to see? Let us know in the comments!

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox's Wild Card clinching ceremony included the usual champagne showers and dripping-wet interviews. Everyone had their moments between the clubhouse party and the team photo, but the expected star of the celebration did not disappont.
Payton Tolle gave Red Sox fans everything they wanted and more out of their playoff-making party. The towering lefty is usually the most hilarious member of the Red Sox, but his antics were turned up to 11 in the presence of more beer than anyone can drink.
Tolle smashed some beers Stone Cold style, danced like no one was watching and gave an under-the-influence interview fans won't soon forget. The best part is that he would probably do many of the same things sober as a judge.
Tolle has grown in to a Red Sox fan favorite in record time. His off-the-field shenanigans match up to the skill he brings on the mound. After his first season-plus with Boston, it should be doing everything in its power to keep Tolle on the team for as long as possible.
Payton Tolle's Wild Card celebration showed just how badly the Red Sox need to extend him
The Red Sox have adopted an early contract extension strategy with many of its young players, including Ceddanne Rafaela, Brayan Bello and Roman Anthony, among others. Alex Speier of The Boston Globe reported on August 18 that Boston hadn't approached Tolle about an extension at the time (subscription required). The Sox have signed so many young players that they could be taking a break, but they should re-start negotiations again for Tolle.
Not only is the 23-year-old an electric personality, he's a force on the mound. The American League's 2026 rookie class is packed to the brim with talent including Kevin McGonigle (the certain winner), Parker Messick and Munetaka Murakami, but Tolle has performed well enough to deserve a mention near the top of this year's list.
Tolle has posted a 3.02 ERA, 1.07 WHIP, 166 strikeouts and 38 walks over 143 innings. The rookie has deepened and sharpened his arsenal this season, his extension (a metric Craig Breslow loves) is elite at a staggering seven-foot-four, his 36.5 percent chase rate sits in the 96th percentile and his 28.9 strikeout percentage ranks near the top of the league. Tolle is an imposing presence on the mound with the prime of his career still years away and the Red Sox should hold onto him for as long as possible.
Tolle will most likely get a start during Boston's Wild Card series, possibly in Game 1. The Red Sox clearly trust him in big moments, he's got personality to share and he's already active in the community — he is the ideal candidate for an early contract extension.

item.title: [heavy.com] Red Sox' Payton Tolle Can Make Franchise History in Postseason
item.dc:creator: Matthew Singer
item.description: The Boston Red Sox are set for a pivotal playoff matchup, likely with the New York Yankees in the first round of the postseason. item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox are set for a pivotal playoff matchup, likely with the New York Yankees in the first round of the postseason.
It’s been a whirlwind of a season for Boston fans after their horrible start under manager Alex Cora and subsequent hot streak under interim manager Chad Tracy. Part of this hot streak has been the emergence of an elite rotation led by rookies and veterans alike.
Their rotation is so good, in fact, that it’s a real discussion of who will start Game 1 and Game 2 between Payton Tolle, Sonny Gray and Ranger Suárez. And it’s a good problem to have!
Rob Bradford of WEEI shared that Tolle has a “good shot” at taking the mound in the first game of the series. If he gets the ball in Game 1 or Game 2, he will make franchise history as the youngest pitcher to start the first or second game of a playoff series since Babe Ruth in the 1918 World Series, per former Red Sox director of baseball communications and media relations JP Long.
Should Boston Red Sox Phenom Payton Tolle Start Game 1 or 2?
The Red Sox drafted Tolle in the second round of the 2024 MLB Draft out of Texas Christian University. Teams quickly saw that Tolle had the tools to succeed, as he sprinted through the minors.
He would soon have an elite year in the minors in his first professional season, making it all the way to the majors in 2025. However, it was rough sledding for Tolle as he sported a 6.06 ERA in 16.1 major league innings.
Going into 2o26, he was a top-20 prospect. From the start of the season, he has not disappointed. In 25 starts during 20026 (143 innings), Tolle has a 3.02 ERA with 166 strikeouts and just 38 walks.
He has the second-lowest ERA among qualified starters on the team, just behind Sonny Gray. While you could definitely make an argument that the veteran Gray should start Game 1, Tolle has been a monster against the Yankees this season.
In his season debut on April 23, Tolle went six innings, allowing just three hits, one walk, one run and striking out 11 batters. On June 26, he would face New York again, going seven innings and allowing just one hit and two walks with seven strikeouts.
Gray has the regular-season production, postseason experience and fuel, being a former Yankees castoff. However, Tolle seems to be at his best when playing against New York and other AL East teams.
Either way, Tolle will likely be making history not seen since the Great Bambino in over a century.
What About Game 3 and Moving Forward?
Suárez should be locked in for a top-3 start, if necessary. In 27 starts, Suárez has a 3.27 ERA in 143.1 innings with 135 strikeouts. The two-time All-Star is also a formidable playoff pitcher, with a minuscule 1.48 ERA in 11 postseason games.
After him, it gets a bit murkier. While you don’t need a full five-man rotation in the playoffs, it’s likely necessary to have a fourth dependable starter.
Rookie Jake Bennett was cruising through his first dozen career starts. However, in his last seven starts, he has a 5.40 ERA. He may be unlikely to shoulder such a burden in his first postseason. It also complicates things that 2025 Cy Young runner-up Garrett Crochet has been out since late April and will likely be a bullpen arm if and when he returns in 2026.
And perhaps the most shocking positive development has been the improvement of Brayan Bello. In his first 10 games, Bello was a disaster. In his last 15, he has been borderline elite with a 2.98 ERA. This was highlighted by an eight-inning performance on Saturday. If needed, Bello could likely be a starter or bulk reliever in the playoffs.
Whatever the case may be, the Boston Red Sox could be a dangerous team in October, with their monster pitching staff at the head of it all.

item.content:encoded:
We’ve made it to the final week of the regular season. There are still two divisions in the American League up for grabs, a couple of long-shot playoff hopefuls looking to make a last-minute run, and playoff seeding to fight over. It should make for a dramatic end to a great season.
Our power rankings use a modified Elo rating system. If you’re familiar with chess rankings, you’ll know that Elo is an elegant ranking format that measures teams’ relative strength and is very reactive to recent performance. To avoid overweighting recent results during the season, we weigh each team’s raw Elo rank using our coin flip playoff odds (specifically, we regress the playoff odds by 50% and weigh those against the raw Elo ranking, increasing in weight as the season progresses to a maximum of 25%). The weighted Elo ranks are then displayed as “Power Score” in the tables below. As the best and worst teams sort themselves out between now and October, they’ll filter to the top and bottom of the rankings, while the exercise remains reactive to hot streaks and cold snaps. If you’re looking for a visual representation of the ups and downs of your team throughout the season, look no further than the brand new Power Rankings Board in the FanGraphs Lab.
First up are the full rankings, presented in a sortable table. Below that, I’ve grouped the teams into tiers with comments on a handful of clubs. You’ll notice that the official ordinal rankings don’t always match the tiers — there are times where I take editorial liberties when grouping teams together — but generally, the ordering is consistent. One thing to note: The playoff odds listed in the tables below are our standard Depth Charts odds, not the coin flip odds that are used in the ranking formula.
