item.content:encoded:
Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman shared a graphic selfie Sunday after suffering a frightening facial injury from a foul ball during an MLB game.
Bregman was struck during the fourth inning of Chicago's 9-1 win over the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park. Teammate Michael Busch fouled a pitch from Luis Mey, and the ball bounced into Bregman while he stood near the on-deck circle.
Bregman immediately left the game with blood visible on his face. He later underwent hospital testing after the ball struck him near his cheekbone.
The selfie, which he shared on his Instagram, showed significant swelling around Bregman's eye, along with facial cuts and a nosebleed. Especially the area below his eye had turned slightly black. He also included a message for supporters: "Thanks for all the messages, y'all. I'll be back 🙏."
Cubs manager Craig Counsell described the incident as a "terrible, terrible accident." He said the team's priority was getting positive medical results after Bregman was taken to the hospital.
The injury came during an important stretch for Chicago. The Cubs entered Sunday chasing a postseason berth and remained positioned for a National League wild-card spot.
Cubs must manage Alex Bregman's absence carefully
Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman (3) walks off the field after getting hit by a foul ball in the fourth inning in the game against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
Bregman had already contributed during Sunday's game before leaving. He delivered an RBI single in the first inning, helping Chicago build an early lead.
After Bregman exited, Matt Shaw replaced him as a pinch-hitter. Pedro Ramirez shifted to third base while Shaw moved to second.
The Cubs continued producing offensively without their veteran third baseman. Pete Crow-Armstrong hit his 45th home run, while Michael Conforto and Seiya Suzuki also homered.
Chicago now faces a balance between its postseason push and Bregman's recovery. His defensive stability and veteran experience remain valuable during the final week.
Counsell said Bregman's general well-being came before baseball considerations. "I want to get a good report first," the manager said.
Bregman's message offered some optimism, but his return timeline remains unclear. The Cubs will need to await further medical updates before determining his availability.

item.title: [98.5 The Sports Hub] Red Sox punch playoff ticket in Tampa
item.dc:creator: Alex Barth
item.description: ST PETERSBURG, FLORIDA – SEPTEMBER 20: Sonny Gray #54 of the Boston Red Sox and Adley Rutschman #31 of the Boston Red Sox celebrate clinching an AL wild card spot following a loss to the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field on September 20, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida. Mark Taylor/Getty Images The massive turnaround of the 2026 Boston Red Sox hit a major milestone on Sunday afternoon. With results around the league, the Sox clinched a spot in the MLB Playoffs. Entering Sunday, the Red Sox didn't
item.content:encoded:
ST PETERSBURG, FLORIDA – SEPTEMBER 20: Sonny Gray #54 of the Boston Red Sox and Adley Rutschman #31 of the Boston Red Sox celebrate clinching an AL wild card spot following a loss to the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field on September 20, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida.
Mark Taylor/Getty Images
The massive turnaround of the 2026 Boston Red Sox hit a major milestone on Sunday afternoon. With results around the league, the Sox clinched a spot in the MLB Playoffs.
Entering Sunday, the Red Sox didn't even need a win of their own to clinch. That was good news because they failed to get one, falling 5-1 to the American East-leading Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field.
Instead, all eyes turned to Texas, where the Houston Astros were hosting the Atlanta Braves. There, they got the help they needed from some familiar names. Former Red Sox starting pitcher Martin Perez allowed just one run in 4.1 innings, and Mike Yastrzemski, the grandson of Red Sox legend Carl Yastrzemski, drove in three runs in Atlanta's 4-2 victory.
After their game ended, the Red Sox watched the Braves and Astros from their locker room in Tampa. As soon as the final out happened the team kicked off a champagne celebration.
Earlier this season, this seemed like an improbable achievement for the Red Sox. On June 24 the team had a 32-46 record and sat in last place in the entire American League. Since then they're 52-26. According to ESPN, they're the fourth team to make the MLB playoffs after being 14-plus games under .500 in a season in the World Series Era.
Now at 84-72 with six games to go, all that's left to determine is seeding - although there's not much wiggle room there. The Red Sox are five and a half games behind the Yankees, who also own the tiebreaker. On the other end the Sox are four and a half games up on the third Wild Card team, which is currently the Chicago White Sox. However Chicago hasn't clinched yet, with a two and a half game lead on both the Astros and Toronto Blue Jays.
The Red Sox will wrap up the season at home before most likely visiting the Yankees in the Wild Card round. For their final week of the regular season the Sox are off on Monday before hosting the Cleveland Guardians, and then the Chicago Cubs.

item.title: [sentinelandenterprise.com] Mike Yastrzemski’s home run for Braves sends Red Sox to postseason
item.dc:creator: Gabrielle Starr
item.description: The Red Sox were unable to punch their own ticket to the postseason Sunday, as they fell to the Tampa Bay Rays, 5-1, at Tropicana Field. Fortunately, one of their former pitchers, the grandson of one of the greatest players to ever don a Red Sox uniform and Boston’s original major league team did it for them. item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox were unable to punch their own ticket to the postseason Sunday, as they fell to the Tampa Bay Rays, 5-1, at Tropicana Field.
Fortunately, one of their former pitchers, the grandson of one of the greatest players to ever don a Red Sox uniform and Boston’s original major league team did it for them.
With a 4-2 defeat of the Houston Astros late Sunday afternoon, the Atlanta Braves propelled the Red Sox to October.
Left-hander Martin Pérez, who pitched for the 2020-21 Red Sox, started for the Braves and held the Astros to one run, a solo homer by Jose Altuve, over 4 1/3 innings.
But the biggest Boston-connected contribution came from Mike Yastrzemski, grandson of Red Sox icon Carl Yastrzemski and a former Red Sox late-round draft pick out of St. John’s Prep in Danvers, Ma. The younger Yaz’s three-run homer in the sixth gave the Braves an enduring lead, and the Red Sox an in.
His momentous home run also coincided with the 59th anniversary of his grandfather hitting his 41st home run and scoring the go-ahead run to keep the 1967 “Impossible Dream” Red Sox in a first-place tie with the Minnesota Twins in a tight American League pennant race.
The final piece of this New England-centric puzzle was a game-ending strikeout of Astros shortstop Jeremy Pena. The Braves originally drafted him in the 39th round of the 2015 MLB Draft out of Providence’s Classic High School, before the Astros took him in the third round in 2018, out of the University of Maine.
The Red Sox watched the Braves from the visitors’ clubhouse at Tropicana Field, then donned “Clinched” t-shirts and goggles, and went back out to the field to celebrate and give the attendants time to seal the clubhouse in plastic wrap and wheel in the champagne and beer.
Long before the Red Sox played their inaugural season as one of the American League’s eight charter clubs in 1901, Boston had the Braves. The Braves were originally the Red Stockings, their name from their 1871 inception until 1876, when they were renamed the Red Caps until 1882.
The 1914 Boston Braves were the first team in MLB history to reach the postseason after being 14 games under .500 at some point in the season. It was a feat only matched by the 1974 Pittsburgh Pirates and 2005 Astros.
Until Sunday, when the Braves helped the Red Sox become the fourth team to do so.

item.content:encoded:
Este domingo, las Grandes Ligas vivió uno de los momentos más dramáticos en los últimos tiempos. Durante el juego entre los Chicago Cubs y Cincinnati Reds, Alex Bregman tuvo un iniesperado accidente mientras estaba esperando su tirno al bat.
El famoso pelotero estadounidense se encontraba en la zona de calentamiento para batear, cuando Michael Busch estaba en el plato e intentó batear una bola, misma que salió a la zona de foul donde se encontraba Bregman y lo agarró desprevenido. El jugador de Cubs recibió un fuerte impacto en el rostro.
RECOMENDAMOS: ¡Casi lo parten! Aaron Rodgers sufre BRUTAL golpe en derrota de Steelers ante Patriots en la NFL
¿Qué le pasó a Alex Bregman?
Después del penoso accidente que sufrió Alex Bregman, se dio a conocer que el jugador de los Cachorros fue trasladado al hospital, pero no hay muchos detalles de cuál es su estado de salud.
El propio manager de los Cubs, Craig Counsell, aseguró que sabe lo mínimo. El entrenador dejó claro que solo sabía de las heridas que tenía en el rostro, incluso llegó a pensar que le habían roto la nariz.
“Tenía una cortada debajo del ojo. Le sangraba un poco la nariz. Está bastante hinchado. Fue debajo del ojo. Sinceramente, pensé que le había pegado en la nariz. Pensé que se había fracturado la nariz, pero sabía que la pelota le había dado en alguna parte del rostro”.
Por su parte, Alex Bregman mostró en sus redes sociales cómo le quedó el rostro después del tremendo pelotazo que le dieron este domingo.
PUEDE INTERESAR: Isaac del Toro finalizó sexto en prueba contrarreloj del Mundial de Ciclismo 2026
¿Quién es Alex Bregman?
Alexander David Bregman, conocido en las Grandes Ligas como Alex Bregman, se ha consolidado como una de las figuras más completas de la tercera base en la última década de las Major League Baseball (MLB).
El beisbolista se ha caracterizado por su paciencia en el plato, excelente disciplina de bateo y una defensa impecable en la esquina caliente, el infielder estadounidense ha sido una pieza fundamental en la época dorada de los Houston Astros antes de continuar su trayectoria profesional.
Los equipos de Alex Bregman:
- Houston Astros (2016–2024)
- Boston Red Sox (2025)
- Chicago Cubs (2026–presente)

item.title: [Boston Herald] ‘Battle-tested’ Red Sox eager to prove they’re ready for more in postseason
item.dc:creator: Gabrielle Starr
item.description: As the clinch celebration played out in the Tropicana Field visitors’ clubhouse early Sunday evening, the incompleteness of the moment was not lost on the revelling Boston Red Sox. The achievement was dampened, and not only in the literal sense by the champagne with which the Red Sox doused each other and the room. item.content:encoded:
As the clinch celebration played out in the Tropicana Field visitors’ clubhouse early Sunday evening, the incompleteness of the moment was not lost on the revelling Boston Red Sox.
The achievement was dampened, and not only in the literal sense by the champagne with which the Red Sox doused each other and the room. That they had lost the series to the Tampa Bay Rays barely an hour earlier and instead had their ticket punched via an Atlanta Braves victory over the Houston Astros. The Red Sox are 9-9 this month, struggling offensively, without on several injured stars, and are their first postseason round will almost certainly be a rematch of last year’s best-of-three Wild Card series at Yankee Stadium, where they fell to their rivals 2-1.
In other words, there is much work to be done. The Red Sox know it, and they are eager to prove they did not come this far to only go this far.
“This has been a turbulent season,” Red Sox chief baseball officer Craig Breslow told reporters. “This is certainly an accomplishment, but it’s not the primary objective here.”
But neither the recent struggles nor the battles ahead should diminish the magnitude of the overall achievement of getting to this point.
The Red Sox lost American League Cy Young runner-up Garrett Crochet to a shoulder injury in mid-April, and he has yet to return.
They fired manager Alex Cora and several coaches in the middle of a late-April road series in Baltimore, and promoted Triple-A Worcester skipper Chad Tracy and several others from their minor league coaching ranks.
Injuries sidelined star outfielder Roman Anthony and veteran shortstop Trevor Story from early May until the very end of August.
The Red Sox owned their worst home record to start a season since 1932, and were 15 1/2 games out of first in the American League East in June.
On June 24, they fell to 14 games under .500. On Sunday, they became the fourth team in Major League Baseball history to go from as many as 14 games under .500 to the postseason in the same season.
“We needed time, and the time came for us,” veteran first baseman Willson Contreras told his teammates in the clubhouse. “I’m very proud of you all.”
“It’s 162 for a reason,” echoed third baseman Caleb Durbin.
“Obviously, getting where we want to go, but ultimately, what we had to overcome to get here makes it all the more sweet,” Tracy said. “We had a long way to go, and they never stopped, and they didn’t take no for an answer.”
This year looked lost, and the Red Sox managed to save it. They maintained an unshakeable belief in themselves, and it has already taken them to places most of the baseball world doubted it could go.
“Belief, belief, belief,” Contreras told reporters. “That was my main word, and that’s what I did from Day 1.”
The Red Sox are not a perfect team. But they certainly have the grit and gumption to go further than expected, as evidenced by the fact that they have already done so by reaching this point.
“We know how it felt when we left New York at the end of the year,” Story said. “You know how it made me feel. So that stayed with me.”
“They came together, and they found a way to get it done, and they had a long way to go to do it,” Tracy said. “They’re very battle-tested, and I’m super, super proud of them.”
“We don’t care where we play,” Tracy said. “You go back to July, and most people didn’t think we’d even be standing here. So it doesn’t matter where we play.”
“We’re in,” Tracy continued. “You got a ticket to the dance, and now you got to go take care of it there.”
“We’re in, baby,” Story said. “Let’s go.”
“Now, this is the moment,” right-fielder Wilyer Abreu said, “that we (were) waiting for.”

item.title: [NESN] Red Sox Legend’s Grandson Delivers Perfect Twist To Playoff Clincher | NESN
item.dc:creator: Rodney Knuppel
item.description: The Boston Red Sox did not secure their postseason berth with a dramatic Fenway Park home run. They did not even clinch with a victory. Instead, a Yastrzemski sent Boston back to October. Mike Yastrzemski, the grandson of Red Sox legend Carl Yastrzemski, hit the decisive three-run home run in the Atlanta Braves’ 4-2 victory over the Houston Astros on Sunday. item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox did not secure their postseason berth with a dramatic Fenway Park home run. They did not even clinch with a victory.
Instead, a Yastrzemski sent Boston back to October.
Mike Yastrzemski, the grandson of Red Sox legend Carl Yastrzemski, hit the decisive three-run home run in the Atlanta Braves’ 4-2 victory over the Houston Astros on Sunday. Houston’s loss officially clinched an American League wild-card berth for Boston.
It was an incredible baseball twist. The younger Yastrzemski has never played for the Red Sox, but his biggest swing of the season delivered an enormous favor to the franchise his grandfather represented for 23 years.
Yastrzemski Produces Perfect Ending For Boston
The Braves and Astros were tied when Yastrzemski came to the plate in the sixth inning. He delivered a three-run homer that gave Atlanta a lead it never relinquished. The victory secured the National League East championship for the Braves and simultaneously eliminated Houston’s remaining path to catching Boston.
The result sent the Red Sox to the playoffs shortly after their disappointing 5-1 loss to the Tampa Bay Rays. Boston could not complete the job itself Sunday. Yastrzemski completed it from Houston. Carl Yastrzemski spent his entire career with the Red Sox. He won the 1967 American League Triple Crown and MVP Award, collected 3,419 hits and became one of the most recognizable players in franchise history.
His grandson’s connection to Boston has followed him throughout his major league career.
That connection suddenly became part of Red Sox history Sunday.
Mike Yastrzemski’s home run was primarily a championship moment for Atlanta. It helped the Braves clinch their seventh division title in nine seasons and earned them a home series to begin the postseason. It also ended an agonizing wait for Boston.
MORE: Red Sox Make MLB History After Season Once Looked Lost
Rough Start For Boston
The Red Sox started the season 32-46 before producing one of baseball’s most remarkable turnarounds. They entered Sunday needing either a victory or an Astros loss to secure their postseason berth.
The victory never came.
The Astros loss did, courtesy of a name forever associated with Boston baseball.
The Red Sox are headed back to October, and a Yastrzemski helped make it happen one more time.

item.title: [BoSox Injection] The Red Sox should take advantage of Garrett Whitlock's desire to start in 2027
item.dc:creator: Stephen Parello
item.description: Garrett Whitlock is looking to make a career pivot and transition into the starting rotation. For the Boston Red Sox, it's a strange proposition. The right-hander is one of the best setup men in the league, and that has tremendous value. Of course, starting pitchers have even more value, hence the higher salaries, but the transition is a risk. item.content:encoded:
Garrett Whitlock is looking to make a career pivot and transition into the starting rotation. For the Boston Red Sox, it's a strange proposition. The right-hander is one of the best setup men in the league, and that has tremendous value.
Of course, starting pitchers have even more value, hence the higher salaries, but the transition is a risk. Not only does a hurler need to reserve something in the tank rather than just air it out for an inning, but he also needs to have enough variation in his arsenal to turn over a lineup multiple times.
Some Red Sox beat writers don't believe the transition is the best idea. The biggest concern is whether or not Whitlock's health can hold up under a starter's workload. The 30-year-old's past forays into starting have resulted in injuries, making this a serious concern and not just some folks crying wolf.
However, there are still reasons to give it a try. Not now, of course. But in 2027, Whitlock in the rotation could make a lot of sense for a few distinct reasons.
The Red Sox should roll the dice on Garrett Whitlock as a starter in 2027
Presumably, the reason Whitlock would like to try his hand again in the rotation is monetary. On the free-agent market, mid-rotation starters can get upwards of $15 million per season. Look at guys like Chris Bassit and Merrill Kelly, for example, who are making $18.5 million and $18 million this season, respectively.
However, Boston holds options for 2027 and 2028 on Whitlock. If exercised, the Red Sox will pay him $8.25 million next year and $10.5 million in 2028. If he works out as a starter, that's an incredible value.
The next reason to give this a go is the fact that Whitlock has the repertoire to work in the rotation. While the majority of relievers are one-or-two-pitch pitchers, Whitlock has three quality offerings. His sinker is the cornerstone, which he throws 56% of the time, but he has a slider and changeup, too.
The slider he uses at a 26% rate, and it generates a ton of whiffs, coming in at 46.7%. The change gets broken out at an 18% clip, is a weapon against lefties, and also has a healthy 35.6% whiff rate. You might like to see a fourth pitch, just to have a show-me offering, but that's a solid foundation for a starter.
The next point is about righty-lefty balance. The Red Sox have an extreme imbalance towards southpaws. Theoretically, if everyone is healthy, you have Garrett Crochet, Ranger Suarez, Payton Tolle, and Jake Bennett all throwing from the left side. If Sonny Gray retires, Boston will have to find a righty to avoid skewing entirely left-handed.
Finally, the risk is minimal. As long as he doesn't suffer a catastrophic injury, the Red Sox can always stick Whitlock back in the bullpen and have a dominant high-leverage reliever should he struggle as a starter. In that regard, they're playing with house money. They control his future for the next two years, and he's paid a reasonable rate for a setup man, and what would be a steal for a No. 3 or No. 4 starter. At that point, why not take the plunge?

item.content:encoded:
The final road game of the 2026 regular season is upon us, as the Yankees will conclude it with a seven-game homestand before likely hosting the Red Sox for the Wild Card Series. If the season ends there, this is the end of the line for the gray uniforms for 2026, but obviously, we all hope we’ll see them next in Tampa (and more) in early October.
Looking to end a road slate that has been very generous to the Yankees on a high note is Will Warren, who’s finishing his sophomore season strong after his great start to the campaign unraveled into a bit of a mess over the summer. Rotation reinforcements that threatened to throw him in the bullpen never came with the recurring injuries, so he’ll finish 2026 with 30 starts for the second straight season. This is No. 29, as he enters with a 3.89 ERA (108 ERA+) and 4.07 FIP in 148 innings. No matter what happens from here, Warren has had a successful year in solidifying himself as a true MLB-caliber rotation arm.
Opposing him will be a former Cy Young winner trying to round into form off Tommy John surgery in Corbin Burnes, whom Yankees fans remember well from his lone season in Baltimore in 2024. Returning from a 16-month absence on September 8 to help with the playoff push, Burnes has allowed five runs across 7.2 innings with six strikeouts to two walks against the Royals and Marlins. He isn’t totally built up, having thrown 75 pitches in his last start, so expect him to settle around 80-85 today. He’s always befuddled the Yankees, pitching to a 1.93 ERA across 23.1 innings in his career, but he doesn’t have a win in any of those four starts.
Ben Rice will once again lead off, followed by Cody Bellinger, Heliot Ramos, and Luis García Jr. We’ve seen better ABs and swings from George Lombard Jr. lately, who’ll bat fifth. Spencer Jones is back after a one-day absence due to a sore foot and will bat in front of Anthony Volpe, Austin Wells, and José Caballero.
Lars Nootbaar will also be a repeat leadoff hitter for the D-backs, followed by Ketel Marte, Gabriel Moreno, and Geraldo Perdomo. Corbin Carroll is batting fifth, Nolan Arenado will bat sixth, and former Blue Jay Jesús Sánchez bats seventh ahead of last night’s hero Pavin Smith and Tim Tawa.
How to watch
Location: Chase Field, Phoenix, AZ
First pitch: 4:10 pm E.T.
TV broadcast: YES, DBACKS.TV
Radio broadcast: WFAN 660/101.9 FM, WADO 1280 (NYY), ESPN 620 AM, La Campesina 101.9 FM & 860 AM (AZ)
Online stream: MLB.tv (out-of-market only), Gotham Sports App

Caleb Durbin’s clutch homer started
item.content:encoded:
April 23: Payton Tolle didn’t make the team out of camp, but was recalled and proved he was ready to stay, allowing one run while striking out 11 against the Yankees
April 25-26: Hours after a 17-1 win in Baltimore, Alex Cora was fired due to his team’s slow start and Chad Tracy, named interim manager, led the team to a 5-3 win in debut the next day
June 25: Airplane issues forced the team to land in Boston at 5 a.m. with a game against the Yankees that night. Caleb Durbin’s clutch homer started the team’s dramatic surge back from 14 games under .500
July 12: The Sox rallied back in the ninth to cap their first 9-0 road trip since 1977. A nine-game winning streak was a nice way to go into All-Star break
July 18: A late-game, go-ahead homer by Wilyer Abreu electrified Fenway and led the Sox to a dramatic comeback win over the Rays to stretch the winning streak to 12 games
July 22: WIth a 6-3 win in Game 1 of a doubleheader against Baltimore, the Red Sox tie a franchise record set by the ‘46 team with a 15-game winning streak
Aug. 2: Hot as hot gets already, the Red Sox opened even more eyes when they completed a three-game sweep of the Dodgers with an 8-4 win on Sunday Night Baseball
Aug. 6: The game that defined a 27-3 stretch that ended two days later, the Red Sox scored in the ninth, 10th, 11th and 12th to finally beat the White Sox, 12-11
Sept. 13: Payton Tolle overpowered the Royals with an immaculate first inning, going almost exclusively with fastballs. And the grin on his face before the ninth pitch said it all

item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — The Red Sox will start Payton Tolle, Sonny Gray, and Ranger Suarez in the series against the Guardians that starts Tuesday at Fenway Park.
That would conceivably line them up for the Wild Card Series that starts on Sept. 29 with six days rest each.
“Don’t read into that yet,” interim manager Chad Tracy said Sunday before a 5-1 loss against the Rays. “We can line that up still however we want.”
True. But Tolle has a 2.44 ERA in his last eight starts. He also has faced the Yankees twice this season and allowed one run on four hits over 13 innings with three walks and 18 strikeouts.
Gray allowed three runs on nine hits over 13⅔ innings in two starts against the Yankees. He struck out 12 and walked three.
Guerrero returns
Righthanded reliever Tyron Guerrero returned from a 19-day stint on the injured list with shoulder inflammation. Righthanded reliever Wyatt Olds was optioned to Triple-A Worcester.
Guerrero pitched a perfect eighth inning, striking out two.
“Felt good to be out there,” Guerrero said. “If I get a few more games I’ll be fine [for the postseason].”
Guerrero, 35, was called up in May for his first major league stint since 2019. He emerged as a reliable late-inning option, posting a 3.18 ERA over 39 games.
“He’s obviously a very important piece to this puzzle in our bullpen,” Tracy said.
Olds deserved a better fate. The 27-year-old has a 1.20 ERA and 1.20 WHIP in 13 games since making his major league debut on Aug. 17.
“Very tough. He’s thrown the ball great. He’s got big stuff,” Tracy said. “We had to make a roster decision.”
Contreras doing better
Willson Contreras took some swings in the batting cage to test his bruised right hand and came through fine. He said he hopes to be able to do more on Tuesday. “Step in the right direction,” Tracy said … There was no update on Garrett Crochet, who has yet to face hitters. That could come in the next few days … Tanner Houck had a 3.38 ERA over eight innings in four minor league games. Tracy suggested he would face hitters in a simulated game early this week. “Figuring out the next steps at home — and want to figure that out — but no plans for the next outing,” Tracy said. Could Houck be activated? “It’s possible,” Tracy said. “At this point, it’s going to depend very much on where’s the roster at, what are the needs, and then go from there.”… Rays shortstop Taylor Walls showed his baseball acumen in the first inning. With Roman Anthony on first and one out, he allowed Adley Rutschman’s popup to drop. Walls picked up the ball and flipped to second to get the force on Anthony. That left the Sox with a slower runner on first. It ultimately didn’t matter as Trevor Story struck out … Worcester, as Double-A Portland also did last weekend, had its final game rained out. The WooSox finished 76-67. Kutter Crawford was at Polar Park, and the plan was to have him start what would have been a bullpen game. Crawford has not appeared in a major league game since Sept. 28, 2024. He missed the 2025 season because of an injured right knee. He injured his right wrist in August of that season doing yard work at his home in Florida. Crawford pitched three innings in a rehab game for Worcester on April 11 but had a setback and wasn’t cleared for a game until Sunday. “He got to a point where he wanted to go out there and throw one,” Tracy said.
Peter Abraham can be reached at peter.abraham@globe.com. Follow him on Bluesky at peteabeglobe.bsky.social.

item.title: [mlb.com] Red Sox clinch postseason spot that once seemed improbable
item.dc:creator: Ian Browne
item.description: Not long after, the Braves beat the Astros, officially punching Boston’s ticket to the playoffs as one of the AL’s three Wild Card teams. It’s a postseason appearance few saw coming when the Sox started the season 32-46. Not only are they the first team in history to advance to finish above .500 after losing as many as 32 of their first 78 games, but now they have a postseason berth to go with it. Currently sitting as the No. 5 seed, the Red Sox are most likely to open their playoff run with a b
item.content:encoded:
Not long after, the Braves beat the Astros, officially punching Boston’s ticket to the playoffs as one of the AL’s three Wild Card teams.
It’s a postseason appearance few saw coming when the Sox started the season 32-46. Not only are they the first team in history to advance to finish above .500 after losing as many as 32 of their first 78 games, but now they have a postseason berth to go with it.
Currently sitting as the No. 5 seed, the Red Sox are most likely to open their playoff run with a best-of-three Wild Card Series at Yankee Stadium, starting on Sept. 29. It would be a rematch from last year, when the Yankees won in three games after the Sox had taken the opener behind a brilliant performance by Garrett Crochet.
In a bit of baseball poetry, a home run swing from Mike Yastrzemski, the grandson of Red Sox legend Carl, gave the Braves a lead they would not relinquish and helped officially push Boston into the postseason.
“When you work as hard as we have worked, it was almost July [before we got going], and to fight as hard as we did, to put ourselves in the position we did, I don’t think you care much how it gets done,” said interim manager Chad Tracy, who took over after the dismissal of Alex Cora on April 25. “You just want to see your ticket get punched.”
For several weeks, the Red Sox never stopped punching. The road back to contention started with a four-game sweep of the Yankees at Fenway from June 25-28.
It continued on July 3, when the Sox began what would become a winning streak of 15 games, tying the franchise record set by the 1946 pennant winners of Ted Williams, Bobby Doerr, Dom DiMaggio and Johnny Pesky.
And even after that streak was snapped, the Sox shortly thereafter ripped off another nine-game winning streak, giving them the best 30-game stretch in team history. Including the Yankees sweep that started it all, Boston was 32-5 from June 25-Aug. 7.
Just when the rabid fanbase known as Red Sox Nation thought they were losing their summer, Boston pulled off one of the most remarkable turnarounds in history, and got the first reward for that on Sunday.

item.title: [BoSox Injection] Roman Anthony headlines loaded Bowman Chrome checklist that should get Red Sox fans excited

item.content:encoded:
If you're not already a card collector, Red Sox fans, here's the quick version of what product sports cards enthusiasts are going crazy over right now. Bowman Chrome is Topps' flagship prospect release, the one product every year built specifically around getting a player's first-ever card into the hobby before he's played a single big-league game. Think of it like a company's IPO. It's the first moment the public gets to invest or collect a piece of a player’s career, before anyone really knows what it'll become.
That's the appeal, and it's also the risk. Some of these names turn into stars. Some never sniff the majors at all. Either way, this is the top of the sports card market right now, and some of these prices have gotten astronomical. You have to truly believe in these prospects to justify what you're paying for a shot at them.
The 1st Bowman class, Roman Anthony rookie cards, and how to collect Red Sox legends
Boston has four 1st Bowman cards this year, all likely the cheapest they’ll ever be simply because nobody outside the organization and minor league baseball enthusiasts know most of these names yet. Here's a rough rule of thumb worth keeping in mind: the higher the signing bonus, the more attention collectors tend to pay, and that logic really kicks in once a bonus crosses $750,000. If a front office was willing to bet that kind of money on a teenager's upside, it's a fair question why a collector wouldn't take the same signal seriously.
Dawvris Brito signed for $1.2 million as the headliner of the 2026 international class, a shortstop with quick-twitch athleticism and triple-digit exit velocities already, and if there is a speculative play, I’d be playing in Brito’s camp. Garielvin Silverio signed for $1.4 million as a physical, left-handed-hitting corner outfielder with raw power, but is likely limited to a corner outfield spot due to lack of speed and athleticism.
Louis Andujar is the wild card of the group, and exactly the kind of story that makes chasing a bargain fun. Boston signed him for just $20,000 out of the Dominican Republic, a number so modest he barely registered outside the organization. He quietly hit .280 with a .974 OPS in the Dominican Summer League, then hit .410 with a 1.233 OPS in his stateside debut this year, good enough for FCL Hitter of the Week honors. If the $750,000 rule (that I made up completely) tells you who the industry believes in, Andujar is the opposite bet entirely, a near-free flier already outplaying his price tag.
The last name in this class comes with the best story attached. Enddy Azocar signed with Boston in January 2024 for just $40,000 out of Venezuela. He climbed all the way to the Red Sox's No. 5 prospect by this summer, hitting .286 with 18 home runs and 11 stolen bases in 85 games, right before Boston shipped him to Baltimore in the Rutschman trade. He hasn't missed a beat since, hitting .467 with a 1.238 OPS in his first 15 at-bats for High-A Frederick, and he's now the Orioles' No. 8 prospect. His 1st Bowman card will always have a Red Sox jersey, a snapshot of the last piece of a $40,000 bet Boston made and then dealt away for a franchise catcher.
Connelly Early carries that same wrinkle in a smaller way. Boston shipped him to the Nationals this July in the Curtis Mead deal, yet his Red RC in this release still has him in a Red Sox uniform. If you're a true Red Sox fan who likes owning a piece of the ones that got away, these are exactly those cards.
If you’re a top prospect hunter and have slept on Franklin Arias, this release gives you more chances to buy into his market, just not the way you'd expect. He doesn't get a 1st Bowman card this year (his 1st came last year), but he shows up with a prospect auto and two inserts as one of the sport's top prospects. If his original 1st Bowman wave passed you by, this is a more affordable way back into his market before he's an everyday big leaguer.
If you believe in Roman Anthony, the rest of this checklist is built for you. This year has been riddled with injury, a hand issue that kept him out for months. But zoom out. Boston signed this guy to an eight-year, $130 million extension back in August 2025, running through 2033 with a 2034 option and escalators that could push the value to $230 million.
That's a franchise betting on a 22-year-old being the face of this roster for the next decade, and Anthony's Red RC, Chrome Rookie Auto, Jumbo Chrome Autograph Relic, and Across the Seams autograph all reflect that same belief. If you're the kind of collector who buys into a player rather than a single season, the injury noise shouldn't scare you off so much as it should make this exact window the moment to buy in, before he's healthy and the price reflects it.
Every team in this release gets a shot at the future. Not every team has the history and memories that Red Sox fans have and names like Manny Ramirez, Roger Clemens, and Pedro Martínez in the same checklist should be like a slice of heaven. Ramirez lands in the Bowman Garbage Pail Kids (GPK) insert, a fitting nod to one of the most feared right-handed bats this franchise has ever run out. Clemens goes a step further with a base GPK card and an autograph version, and Pedro shows up in the Final Draft insert. None of these are prospect chases, and none will likely come cheap either, but they're closer to a tribute set than an investment. For a fanbase that grew up on these names, that's a fun thing to pull, regardless of cost.
Prices are always inflated in the first few weeks. Anthony's cards will likely cost the most, so waiting a month for the market to settle isn't unreasonable if you're patient. But Brito, Silverio, Azocar, and Andujar are cheap speculative buys worth grabbing now, and the Manny, Clemens, and Pedro pulls are worth paying up for if the fun of the rip matters more to you than the price tag.

item.title: [tsn.ca] Cubs’ Bregman exits after being hit in face by foul ball while in on-deck circle
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.description: CINCINNATI (AP) — Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman was taken to the hospital for tests after being struck in the face by a foul ball while standing in the grass several feet in front of the on-deck circle during Sunday’s game against the Cincinnati Reds. item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI (AP) — Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman was taken to the hospital for tests after being struck in the face by a foul ball while standing in the grass several feet in front of the on-deck circle during Sunday’s game against the Cincinnati Reds.
There was no decision yet on whether Bregman, who was going for X-rays and CT scans, would travel with the team back to Chicago following its 9-1 win.
“He got hit in the left cheekbone essentially, under the eye,” Cubs manager Craig Counsell said. “I don’t know anything more than that right now. He was bleeding from his nose a little. There’s some swelling. It’s a terrible, terrible accident. We hope he’s OK.”
In the fourth inning, left-handed batting Michael Busch checked his swing and fouled off a pitch from Reds right-hander Luis Mey that struck Bregman, who immediately jogged toward the Cubs' dugout with his hand covering the left side of his face.
Bregman was escorted by a trainer down the dugout steps and into the clubhouse, with blood visible on his face. Matt Shaw replaced Bregman and drew a walk. He remained in the game to play second base, with Pedro Ramirez shifting to third.
“It just happens so fast,” Busch said. “(Mey)'s throwing the ball hard and it comes off hard. Any time it enters the head area, it's always a scary thing. We try to focus on the game, but it's tough. Hopefully he's OK, first and foremost.”
Bregman went 1 for 1 with a walk, an RBI and a run scored before leaving the game. He is batting .262 with 26 home runs and 89 RBIs after signing a $175 million, five-year free agent deal in January.
“I mean, at the end of the day, you just hope your friend is OK,” Pete Crow-Armstrong said. “That's the news that I'm hoping for. But scary stuff. Such a rarity.”
The Cubs could clinch a postseason berth with a Diamondbacks loss to the Yankees later Sunday.
Counsell said he hasn't thought about how a potential long-term absence for Bregman might impact his postseason roster plans.
“You know, we've got to get good results from the hospital,” Counsell said. “He got hit in the face (so) you're worried just about his general well-being first. I want to get a good report first.”
___
See AP’s full MLB coverage here
Jeff Wallner, The Associated Press

item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (AP) — Griffin Jax tossed five shutout innings and the Tampa Bay Rays crept closer to the AL East title with a 5-1 victory over the Boston Red Sox on Sunday. item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (AP) — Griffin Jax tossed five shutout innings and the Tampa Bay Rays crept closer to the AL East title with a 5-1 victory over the Boston Red Sox on Sunday.
The Rays will have an opportunity to clinch the franchise’s fifth division title during Tuesday’s doubleheader at the New York Yankees.
Despite the loss, the Red Sox later secured a playoff berth when the Houston Astros lost to the Atlanta Braves. The Red Sox waited out the Astros-Braves result and held a celebration in their clubhouse. The Red Sox, who were 32-46 and 15 1/2 games back in the AL East on June 24, have since gone 52-25.
Jax (8-10) allowed three singles and worked out of a bases-loaded jam in the fifth inning by striking out Roman Anthony. Cole Sulser, Brody Hopkins and Steven Matz each pitched an inning of scoreless relief.
Boston’s Trevor Story spoiled the shutout in the ninth with a one-out home run off right-hander Ty Johnson.
The Rays scored four first-inning runs off left-hander Patrick Sandoval (1-7). Jonny DeLuca smashed a two-run, bases-loaded double down the left-field line and Chandler Simpson followed with a two-run single. Sandoval began the inning by walking Yandy Diaz and Ryan Vilade, then surrendering a single to Junior Caminero.
Sandoval then retired 21 of his next 23 batters and worked through the seventh inning, allowing only a first-inning walk and a fourth-inning homer, both to Victor Mesa Jr.
Up next
After a day off Monday, Boston will start LHP Payton Tolle (9-6, 3.02) at home against the Cleveland Guardians. Right-hander Nick Martinez (15-4, 2.94) is set to start the opener of the doubleheader in New York, while right-hander Drew Rasmussen (15-5, 2.72) to pitch Game 2.
___
See AP’s full MLB coverage here
The Associated Press

item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI (AP) — Pete Crow-Armstrong hit his 45th home run as the Chicago Cubs moved closer to clinching a postseason berth with a 9-1 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Sunday.
Chicago (87-69) reduced its magic number to one and could wrap up a berth if the Diamondbacks lose to the Yankees later Sunday.
The Cubs began the day tied with the Padres and one game ahead of the Phillies for the top NL wild-card spot which would earn them home-field advantage in the wild-card round. The Cubs own the tiebreakers over the Diamondbacks, Padres, and Phillies.
Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman left Sunday’s game in the fourth inning after being struck in the face by a foul ball off the bat of Michael Busch while standing near the on-deck circle.
Cubs left-hander David Peterson (9-8) allowed a run on three hits in seven innings with one walk and seven strikeouts.
The Cubs loaded the bases with one out in the third. Ian Happ singled in a run and Nico Hoerner walked to force in another to extend Chicago’s lead to 3-0. Pedro Ramirez’s two-run single made the score 5-0.
Reds right-hander Rhett Lowder (6-12) allowed five earned runs on six hits with three walks and three strikeouts.
Michael Conforto’s 15th home run made the score 6-1 in the fifth. Three batters later, Crow-Armstrong’s two-run home run made it 8-1.
Seiya Suzuki hit his 25th homer of the season in the eighth.
JJ Bleday hit his 23rd home run of the season for Cincinnati. Reds right-hander Carson Spiers allowed four runs and three homers in four innings. He also struck out five.
Up next
Cubs: Have not announced a starter for Tuesday’s series opener against the Marlins.
Reds: LHP Andrew Abbott (6-11, 4.70) is scheduled to start Tuesday in Atlanta.
___
See AP’s full MLB coverage here
Jeff Wallner, The Associated Press

item.title: [bignewsnetwork.com] AL-best Rays complete 8-1 homestand by stifling Red Sox
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.description: AL-best Rays complete 8-1 homestand by stifling Red Sox (Photo credit: Pablo Robles) Tampa Bay's Jonny DeLuca and Chandler Simpson drove in a pair apiece in a four-run first inning, Victor Mesa Jr. homered and the Rays won for the eighth time in their final regular-season homestand by beating the Boston Red Sox 5-1 on Sunday afternoon in St. Petersburg, Fla. In finishing 8-1 on their last homestand before the postseason, the Rays (95-60) sent nine batters to the plate in the first and never look
item.content:encoded:
AL-best Rays complete 8-1 homestand by stifling Red Sox
(Photo credit: Pablo Robles)
Tampa Bay's Jonny DeLuca and Chandler Simpson drove in a pair apiece in a four-run first inning, Victor Mesa Jr. homered and the Rays won for the eighth time in their final regular-season homestand by beating the Boston Red Sox 5-1 on Sunday afternoon in St. Petersburg, Fla.
In finishing 8-1 on their last homestand before the postseason, the Rays (95-60) sent nine batters to the plate in the first and never looked back as they concluded their home schedule with a majors-best 55-26 mark.
Starter Griffin Jax (8-10) fired five scoreless frames with three hits allowed. He fanned five with two walks over 74 offerings.
Trevor Story homered, and Roman Anthony (double) and Caleb Durbin each went 2-for-4. However, Boston (84-72) managed only six hits in losing its second straight.
Starter Patrick Sandoval (1-7) rebounded from a terrible beginning to finish seven innings, allowing five runs on four hits. He struck out five, walked two and hit a batter in 94 pitches.
Tampa Bay put its first five batters on base against Sandoval, and DeLuca doubled in two runs before Simpson singled in two more as the Rays batted around in the first.
Jax was dialed in early after yielding a leadoff single to Anthony. The right-hander retired 10 straight batters, four by strikeouts, until Adley Rutschman singled with one out in the fourth.
In the bottom of the fourth, Mesa made it 5-0 by cranking Sandoval's 95 mph four-seamer out to right-center a Statcast-estimated 403 feet. It was the right fielder's 14th home run.
The Red Sox had a chance to get back in it by loading the bases in the fifth on a single by Durbin and two walks, but Anthony -- who drove in five of the club's six runs in the series -- whiffed to end it on a sinking 2-2 changeup from Jax, the starter's final pitch.
With a fire alarm going off behind center field causing a short delay, Cole Sulser tossed a perfect sixth as the bullpen began its stretch of four innings of one-run work.
Story hit his fifth homer with one out in the ninth to spoil the shutout.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [Boston Herald] First-inning implosion costs Red Sox chance to punch own postseason ticket
item.dc:creator: Gabrielle Starr
item.description: The Boston Red Sox woke up on Sunday knowing they could punch their ticket to the postseason in one of two ways. They could beat the Tampa Bay Rays in their series finale, or the Atlanta Braves could defeat the Houston Astros in theirs. A first-inning shellacking put Boston’s fate in the Braves’ hands, as the Rays ultimately took the series with a 5-1 victory. Left-hander Patrick Sandoval needed 40 pitches to complete the nine-batter frame. The first five Rays reached, and put up a 4-0 lead on b
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox woke up on Sunday knowing they could punch their ticket to the postseason in one of two ways.
They could beat the Tampa Bay Rays in their series finale, or the Atlanta Braves could defeat the Houston Astros in theirs.
A first-inning shellacking put Boston’s fate in the Braves’ hands, as the Rays ultimately took the series with a 5-1 victory.
Left-hander Patrick Sandoval needed 40 pitches to complete the nine-batter frame. The first five Rays reached, and put up a 4-0 lead on back-to-back two-run base hits by centerfielder Jonny DeLuca (double) and left-fielder Chandler Simpson (single) before the Red Sox starter could record an out. Sandoval issued his second walk of the inning to Victor Mesa Jr. before he finished the frame and stranded two runners.
“Nightmare, like legit nightmare situation,” a grimacing Sandoval told reporters postgame of the first inning. “Couldn’t really where my arm was in space, grip on the ball wasn’t great. Just a literal nightmare.”
Then came a complete 180. Sandoval looked like a new man when he returned for the bottom of the second. He set the Rays down in order on eight pitches, then needed six to do so again in the third.
Sandoval retired eight consecutive Rays before Mesa homered with one out in the fourth to push the lead to five. But it marked Tampa Bay’s fourth and final hit of the day; Sandoval retired his last 11 batters, and newly-returned righty Tyron Guerrero extended the streak to 14 with a 1-2-3 eighth.
Yet the Red Sox, who left 17 men on base over the first two games of the series, were blanked by righty Griffin Jax and the Rays bullpen until a brief rally bid in the top of the ninth. Boston out-hit Tampa Bay 6-4, but went 0 for 4 with runners in scoring position, and stranded six.
Roman Anthony led off the game with a groundball single to right, but he was erased and replaced when catcher Adley Rutschman popped into a force out. The Red Sox did not put another man on base until Rutschman singled with one out in the fourth, an opportunity quickly erased by shortstop Trevor Story grounding into an inning-ending double play.
Boston’s best chance came and went in Jax’s fifth and final frame, when they loaded the bases on a one-out single by third baseman Caleb Durbin, and walks to centerfielder Jarren Duran and right-fielder Nate Eaton. Jax, who had not exceeded 67 pitches in a start since Aug. 2, was up to 69 when Anthony came to bat with two outs and the bases loaded. It took five pitches to end the threat; Anthony swung and missed at Jax’s last two, a 95.3 mph sinker and 90.2 mph changeup.
Much like Saturday’s 2-1 loss, Boston had no hope against the Tampa Bay bullpen. The Red Sox went in order against Cole Sulser in the sixth, and Brody Hopkins in the seventh.
Facing 2025 Red Sox trade deadline acquisition Steven Matz in the eighth, Anthony doubled with two outs. Jahmai Jones came in to pinch-hit for designated hitter Mickey Gasper. Jones has dominated left-handed pitching since the Red Sox acquired him from the Detroit Tigers during the All-Star break, but Matz struck him out swinging on four pitches.
After his 40-pitch first, Sandoval completed his remaining six innings on a mere 54. He became just the fourth Red Sox pitcher in the last 26 years, and first since Rick Porcello in 2016, to pitch at least seven innings after giving up at least four runs in the first. Sandoval yielded five earned runs on four hits, walked two (both in the first), and struck out five over seven innings. He threw 73.4% of his 94 pitches for strikes.
Activated from the injured list Sunday morning, Guerrero was sharp in his first inning of work since Aug. 31. The towering righty retired the Rays’ No. 2-4 batters, including American League home-run leader Junior Caminero, in order on 12 pitches (nine strikes). Guerrero’s return will bolster a Boston bullpen currently without closer Aroldis Chapman (day-to-day with lat tightness), and righty Justin Slaten (season-ending flexor injury).
Story ensured the Red Sox would not be shut out. His fifth home run of the year, off righty Ty Johnson, soared 405 feet to left at 102.7 mph with one out in the ninth.
Thus concludes the final Red Sox road trip of the season. They went 2-4 against the Texas Rangers and Rays, were outscored 23-15, and left 42 men on base.
After an off-day Monday, their final homestand of the season begins Tuesday night against the Cleveland Guardians.
But first, all eyes turn to the Braves and Astros.

item.content:encoded:
Boston Red Sox right-hander Kutter Crawford was set to make a rehab start with Triple-A Worcester. But with the game being cancelled due to rain, per the Worcester Telegram-Gazette's Tommy Cassell, the club faces a tough roster decision on the 30-year-old starter.
The cancellation also ends Worcester's season. That means the Red Sox will have to decide if they want to roster Crawford during the final seven games of the regular season, and possibly the postseason.
Crawford is currently on the 60-day injured list after suffering a major setback in his recovery from wrist surgery. After a rehab start in April, he experienced issues in his right elbow and has been shelved since. This appearance would have been his first outing in five months.
Red Sox Face Tough Roster Decision on Kutter Crawford
With nowhere to get a rehab outing, the Red Sox will have to decide the next steps for Kutter Crawford. They certainly had some contingency in place if the game was affected by weather.
The first question the Red Sox have to answer is whether Crawford is an option for the postseason. If not, they will likely just shut him down. Otherwise, they have to clear a 40-man roster spot to activate him from the injured list.
If Boston does roster the 30-year-old, it will likely be in a relief role. The Red Sox will likely go into the Wild Card Series with a three-man rotation of Sonny Gray, Ranger Suarez, and Payton Tolle. If they advance further, they could turn to either Jake Bennett or Brayan Bello as their fourth starter.
Given the postseason in general, there could be some need for an innings-eater for the bullpen. But Bello and Bennett are further stretched out than Crawford at this point in the season.
If Crawford is done for the year, it will mark the second straight season the right-hander has not thrown a pitch for the Red Sox. That could make him a non-tender candidate in November. But if they do tender him, he won't see much of a raise from his $2.75 million salary for 2026.
It's quite possible that Crawford has thrown his last pitch for the Red Sox.
Red Sox Right Now
The Red Sox aim to clinch a postseason berth in their series finale against the Tampa Bay Rays. They'll send left-hander Patrick Sandoval to the mound.
Boston needs a win or a loss by the Houston Astros to officially clinch. They've already been eliminated from American League East contention, so they would be locked into a Wild Card spot.
The Red Sox have a five-game lead for the AL's second Wild Card spot. So they should lock in their postseason seeding in the next couple of days. That would allow them to set up their rotation for the Wild Card Series. Their likely first opponent in the postseason will be the New York Yankees.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Red Sox Face Tough Kutter Crawford Roster Decision After Rehab Start Cancelled appeared first on HEAVY.

item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — The Red Sox have been unerringly diligent about resting players as they prepare for the postseason. But they still haven’t clinched their spot.
They slept through a 5-1 loss against the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field on Sunday, managing only six hits before a crowd of 24,654.
The Sox left the field needing the Braves to beat the Astros to finally clinch their spot.
It has been a slog for a while. The Sox were 2-4 on their road trip and are 11-13 since Aug. 26. They end the regular season with a six-game homestand starting Tuesday against the Guardians.
The Sox scored two runs in the last two games against the Rays and were 1 for 15 with runners in scoring position, leaving 14 men on base.
Griffin Jax (8-10) and five relievers allowed six hits on Sunday. The Sox had a chance to get back in the game in the fifth inning when they loaded the bases with two outs, but Roman Anthony struck out.
Patrick Sandoval (1-7) allowed four runs during a 40-pitch first inning.
The lefthander walked Yandy Díaz on four pitches, then hit Ryan Vilade with a 2-and-2 fastball. Junior Caminero singled to left field to load the bases.
Jonny DeLuca followed with a two-run double to left and Chandler Simpson with a two-run single to right. That was essentially the game as the Sox could not punch back until Trevor Story had a solo home run off Ty Johnson in the ninth inning.
Sandoval completed seven innings and allowed only one more run, on a home run by Victor Mesa Jr. After the long first inning, Sandoval threw 54 pitches over the next six and faced only 19 batters.
Peter Abraham can be reached at peter.abraham@globe.com. Follow him on Bluesky at peteabeglobe.bsky.social.

item.title: [bosoxinjection.com] Wondering how much better the Red Sox would've been in 2026 if not for awful injury luck
item.dc:creator: Colin Keane
item.description: The Boston Red Sox are just a few wins from clinching a playoff spot for the second year in a row following a three-year hiatus. It's been a successful year on paper for the Red Sox, especially given all of their early-season chaos. But it's hard not to wonder... what if this team had been healthier in 2026? Deadline acquisition Curtis Mead barely got to play at all for the Red Sox, and now he could be done for the season. Garrett Crochet made just six starts for Boston. Roman Anthony lost the b
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox are just a few wins from clinching a playoff spot for the second year in a row following a three-year hiatus. It's been a successful year on paper for the Red Sox, especially given all of their early-season chaos. But it's hard not to wonder... what if this team had been healthier in 2026?
Deadline acquisition Curtis Mead barely got to play at all for the Red Sox, and now he could be done for the season. Garrett Crochet made just six starts for Boston. Roman Anthony lost the bulk of what was supposed to be his first full MLB season. Justin Slaten's season is now over prematurely.
Everywhere you look on Boston's '26 roster, there are questions about what could have been. Mead is a potent right-handed bat who was supposed to add not only extra thump to the lineup but also infield depth.
Crochet is a much bigger theoretical. Last year's AL Cy Young runner-up pitched just 30 innings for Boston this season before landing on the IL with shoulder inflammation. In essence, the Red Sox rotation has been missing its true ace for nearly the entire year.
Red Sox's 2026 season comes with a huge "What if?"
Anthony’s absence was also tough to swallow for months. He hit .292/.396/.463 with an 140 OPS+ in 71 games as a 21-year-old in 2025, leading many to crown him Boston's franchise player moving forward. This year he played 30 games, then tore a ligament in his right ring finger on a check swing in early May. It was a freak injury that a hand specialist told reporters he had never seen isolated that way.
The Red Sox couldn't have expected Anthony to miss as much time as he did, and the somewhat mysterious nature of the injury made it impossible to plan for when he'd come back. It was a perpetual "when's he coming back?" buzzkill situation for the organization and its fans for months, not that Anthony is to blame.
Anthony and Crochet's absences alone make one wonder if the Red Sox would have already clinched by now had those two been healthy for most of the season. Certainly the Wild Card, no? The division is a harder argument, based on how good Tampa Bay has been all year. But we can realistically assume that the Red Sox would at least be battling the Yankees for the wild-card lead right now (or better) had Anthony and Crochet played more games.
Alas, that's all water under the bridge, and this roster is still on track for October baseball, thanks to a historic surge after the All-Star break. This is a more patched-together version of the Red Sox than any Boston fan would have preferred, but such is often the consequence of a 162-game marathon. Even so, no matter how Boston fares in the postseason (outside of a run to the World Series), fans will always be asking "What if?" about this year.

item.title: [pinstripealley.com] Yankees Rivalry Roundup: Rays rebound against Red Sox with walk-off
item.dc:creator: Andrew Mearns
item.description: The Yankees’ odds of winning the AL East are down to 2.8 percent per FanGraphs after getting walked off by the Diamondbacks last night. I know mathematically that makes sense, but the chances mentally feel even more extreme. I’ve been having “fun” (or whatever) comping the odds to certain pitchers from history getting a hit.
