Ildemaro Vargas walked to lead off the ninth off Michael Fulmer (0-1), reaching base after he appealed the 3-2 pitch that
item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

20 Sep 2026, 13:49 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Arianna Grainey)
Pinch hitter Pavin Smith hit a two-run, walk-off homer with one out in the ninth and the Arizona Diamondbacks beat the New York Yankees 5-3 on Saturday in Phoenix on a night the franchise celebrated the 25th anniversary of their 2001 World Series victory over the Yankees.
Ildemaro Vargas walked to lead off the ninth off Michael Fulmer (0-1), reaching base after he appealed the 3-2 pitch that originally was called a strike. After a strikeout, Smith hit a 391-foot homer to right center for the D-backs' 46th comeback win of the season
Heliot Ramos and Austin Wells hit bases-empty homers for the Yankees, who had won four of five and eight of 10. Wells and Jose Caballero had two hits apiece.
Nolan Arenado had two hits and Jordan Lawlar added a two-run triple for the D-backs, who had lost three in a row and five of six.
The Yankees (89-65), who have clinched a playoff berth, fell five games behind Tampa Bay (94-60) in the American League East and remained 5 1/2 games ahead of Boston (84-71) for the top AL wild-card spot. The Yankees and Rays play a four-game series in Yankee Stadium beginning with a split doubleheader Tuesday.
White Sox 3, Tigers 1
Sean Burke hurled six quality innings and Miguel Vargas homered to help Chicago earn a victory over visiting Detroit.
Burke (10-7) allowed one run on five hits for Chicago, which remained a game behind American League Central-leading Cleveland. Sam Antonacci and Munetaka Murakami both drove in a run and Grant Taylor delivered a four-out save, his 10th overall this season.
Jackson Jobe (2-3) threw six innings of three-run, four-hit ball, striking out nine for Detroit, which remains barely alive in AL Central contention. The Tigers' wild-card elimination magic number is down to one. Kevin McGonigle drove in Detroit's lone run.
Mets 10, Phillies 3
Francisco Alvarez had two hits, including the go-ahead three-run homer in the fifth, as host New York routed skidding Philadelphia.
Carson Benge was 3-for-4 with a solo homer and two RBIs for the Mets. Brett Baty had two hits, including a run-scoring single, while Benge, Juan Soto and Bo Bichette each had RBI singles during a four-run eighth.
Alec Bohm had RBI singles in the fourth and fifth for the Phillies, who missed a chance to take over the top National League wild card, at least temporarily. The Cubs and Padres both won to remain tied atop the NL wild-card race.
Brewers 1, Orioles 0Robert Gasser pitched seven shutout innings as the first of three Milwaukee pitchers in a victory against host Baltimore.
It marked the second shutout for Milwaukee pitchers in an eight-game stretch, needing only four strikeouts for the latest accomplishment. The Brewers scored on Gary Sanchez's second-inning groundout to knock in Joey Ortiz, who tripled with one out.Baltimore has lost the first two games of the series following a three-game winning streak, further damaging its American League playoff hopes. Orioles starter Trevor Rogers (10-11) lasted eight innings, allowing one run and three hits.
Rangers 6, Blue Jays 2Texas won for the sixth time in its past seven games, defeating Toronto in Arlington, Texas.Rangers starting pitcher Cal Quantrill left the game after 1 1/3 innings with right lat tightness. Jordan Montgomery (1-0) replaced him and held Toronto hitless through 3 2/3 innings. Josh Jung gave Texas a 1-0 lead in the bottom of the first with a home run to right field.Jose Soriano (12-8) gave up six runs (five earned) on four hits and struck out eight in five-plus innings for the Blue Jays, who dropped to three games behind the Chicago White Sox for the final wild-card berth in the American League.
Rays 2, Red Sox 1
Richie Palacios produced a two-out, walk-off single in the ninth inning as Tampa Bay edged Boston in St. Petersburg, Fla., to even their final home series of the regular season.
Against Garrett Whitlock (7-2), Palacios looped a 1-2 sinker into right to score Junior Caminero as the Rays hit their third walk-off winner during their nine-game homestand. Jonathan Aranda homered while Liam Hicks and Chandler Simpson posted two hits apiece.
Caleb Durbin stroked two doubles and scored for the Red Sox, who lost for the first time in three games. Starting pitcher Brayan Bello went a season-best eight innings and allowed one run on five hits with a career high-tying 11 strikeouts.
Guardians 12, Athletics 6
Angel Martinez homered from both sides of the plate and drove in four runs in host Cleveland's win over the Athletics which helped maintain its one-game lead in the American League Central.
Martinez was also 4-for-5 with a double and three runs scored and Chase DeLauter also homered for the Guardians, who won their fourth straight. Slade Cecconi (5-7) got the win in relief with two scoreless innings after Tanner Bibee lasted 4 2/3 innings and surrendered six runs on 12 hits.
Donovan Walton hit a home run and was 3-for-3 with four RBIs for the Athletics, who have lost five in a row. Athletics starter and loser Jacob Lopez (6-5) was blitzed for 10 runs and 10 hits in 2 2/3 innings.
Nationals 8, Cardinals 5 (11 innings)Jose Tena's two-run double keyed a four-run 11th inning and Washington beat the Cardinals in St. Louis.Jorbit Vivas had four hits and Daylen Lile homered for Washington, which has won six of seven. Riley Cornelio (3-2) pitched 1 2/3 innings for the win.At the top of the order, Jose Fermin and Ivan Herrera had three hits each for St. Louis, which has lost four straight.
Cubs 5, Reds 2
Michael Busch and Dansby Swanson hit solo home runs to lift visiting Chicago to a win over Cincinnati.
The win allowed the Cubs to pull a full game ahead of the Philadelphia Phillies for the top wild-card playoff spot in the National League. The Phillies lost 10-3 to the Mets earlier. The San Diego Padres also won to remain tied with the Cubs.
The teams will play the rubber game of the series Sunday. Cubs starter Matthew Boyd (9-5) gave up two hits and two runs (one earned) in five innings. Reds starter Nick Lodolo (3-6) gave up seven hits and three runs in seven innings.
Pirates 6, Royals 5
Brandon Lowe launched a go-ahead two-run home run in the eighth inning to power Pittsburgh to a victory over visiting Kansas City.
Ronny Simon and Jake Mangum each hit two-run homers, while Oneil Cruz, Rafael Flores Jr. and Lowe each had two hits for the Pirates. Right-hander Luke Weaver (3-1) threw a scoreless eighth with one strikeout, and left-hander Mason Montgomery earned his 15th save of the season after working around a walk with one strikeout in a scoreless ninth.
Nick Loftin had four hits, while Bobby Witt Jr. went 3-for-5 with two runs and extended his on-base streak to 17 games for the Royals. Carter Jensen hit a solo homer, while Jac Caglianone and Vinnie Pasquantino each had two hits for Kansas City.
Braves 6, Astros 3Ronald Acuna Jr. hit a grand slam, Grant Holmes produced a quality start and Atlanta lowered its magic number to one to clinch the National League East by defeating host Houston.The Braves secured this three-game interleague series and set the table to win the NL East for the seventh time in nine seasons with a victory in the series finale on Sunday. Holmes (10-5) allowed two runs on eight hits over six innings. Closer Raisel Iglesias notched his 34th save for Atlanta.The Astros dropped a game behind the Rangers in the AL West after Texas beat Toronto. Astros reliever AJ Blubaugh (5-3) loaded the bases and was replaced by Bryan Abreu, who gave up Acuna's homer in the seventh inning for a 5-2 Braves lead.Rockies 5, Mariners 3
Cole Carrigg delivered a go-ahead two-run single in a four-run seventh inning as Colorado edged Seattle in Denver.
Juan Mejia (4-6) pitched two scoreless innings and Brennan Bernardino got the final three outs for his second save for Colorado. Jake McCarthy and TJ Rumfield each produced an RBI.
Cal Raleigh and Randy Arozarena homered and Julio Rodriguez and Michael Arroyo had two hits each for Seattle, which is on the brink of elimination in the AL wild-card race.
Padres 6, Marlins 5 (10 innings)
Rookie Ethan Salas stroked an RBI single in the bottom of the 10th inning and San Diego edged visiting Miami.
Salas' hit scored Jake Cronenworth, who started the inning as the automatic runner at second base and advanced to third on a wild pitch by Josh Ekness (2-4). David Morgan (4-1) stranded runners at first and second in the top of the 10th to earn the win, San Diego's 12th in 13 games.
The Padres tied the Chicago Cubs for the top wild-card spot in the National League at 86-69. Miami forced extra innings when pinch hitter Griffin Conine pulled a 102 mph fastball from closer Mason Miller for a game-tying homer with one out in the ninth.
Dodgers 10, Giants 4
Mookie Betts tied a season high with four hits, Tommy Edman delivered a go-ahead two-run single and Los Angeles stayed within two games of the best record in the National League with a victory over visiting San Francisco.
Betts has 10 hits over his past three games, including seven in the past two while operating out of the leadoff spot in place of an injured Shohei Ohtani. Will Smith homered as the Dodgers won for the fifth time in six games and improved to 13-3 since Sept. 3. Tarik Skubal (11-7) gave up four runs on eight hits over five innings.
Victor Bericoto hit a home run among his two hits for the Giants while Yunior Marte (0-1) gave up six runs on eight hits over 4 2/3 innings in his fourth career appearance and second start.
Angels 6, Twins 5 (11 innings)Christian Moore singled in automatic runner Zach Neto with a bases-loaded comebacker off pitcher Taylor Rogers' leg with two outs in the bottom of the 11th inning as Los Angeles edged Minnesota in Anaheim, Calif.Moore drilled a first-pitch sweeper that caromed off the leg of Rogers (6-4) and back toward the third base line as Neto sprinted home. Tayler Saucedo (1-1) struck out two during a scoreless inning of relief for the Angels, who tied it at 5-5 in the bottom of the ninth on Vaughn Grissom's homer.Ryan Kreidler hit a home run, Victor Caratini went 2-for-5 with two RBIs, Walker Jenkins had two hits and a run and Josh Bell and Royce Lewis each had two hits for the Twins.
--Field Level Media

item.dc:creator: Patrick McAvoy; Unknown
item.description: The Boston Red Sox got another promising day from lefty ace Garrett Crochet on Saturday on his quest back to the big leagues before the 2026 season comes to an end. Crochet hasn't pitched in a game since April 25 due to shoulder/lat injuries. Since then, he has been working his way back and recently has been throwing bullpens. item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox got another promising day from lefty ace Garrett Crochet on Saturday on his quest back to the big leagues before the 2026 season comes to an end.
Crochet hasn't pitched in a game since April 25 due to shoulder/lat injuries. Since then, he has been working his way back and recently has been throwing bullpens. On Saturday, he tossed his latest over in Worcester at Polar Park. Crochet tossed about 20 pitches and reached 92 miles per hour. On top of this, WooSox pitching coach Dan DeLucia gave Boston fans some hope by saying he looked "great," as shared by Tommy Cassell of the Worcester Telegram and Gazette.
"Crochet, dressed in a full white Red Sox uniform, tossed roughly 20 pitches and sat in the 91 to 92 MPH range," Cassell wrote. "'He looks great,' DeLucia said. 'It was pretty much what we expected. Like, that was the expectation, go out there and kind of make it an in-between side start. No, actually probably a tick above what I think the expectations were, but for the most part, as expected the fine-tuning things, getting on the mound again.'"
The Red Sox Got Another Positive Day From Garrett Crochet
So, what should Red Sox fans make of this?
This is yet another positive. At first glance, the 91/92 MPH fastball may jump out to fans. Of course, that's not up to his peak and is approaching 100 MPH. But that's okay. The fact that DeLucia commented on the throwing session and even said that it was "probably a tick" above what they expected is a sign that he's continuing to make the progress the club has hoped for.
When it comes to Crochet, he has been throwing bullpens for weeks at this point. Earlier in the week, he advanced to a multi-inning up-and-down his last time out. The big lefty followed up on Saturday with a lighter workload. Earlier in the week he got up to 30 pitches and followed with another 20, or so, on Saturday.
For Crochet, the biggest thing to watch next will be when he faces live hitters. Facing live batters is the next big step. When he advances to that level, we'll start to get a real view of how he stacks up and whether he truly looks like himself. The current expectation is that a live bullpen will come early next week. The clock is ticking as well. There are just seven games left in the regular season. The playoffs will begin on Sep. 29. Will Crochet be ready by then? It's still possible.
Patrick McAvoy's experiences include local and national sports coverage at the New England Sports Network with a focus on baseball and basketball. Outside of journalism, Patrick received an MBA at Brandeis University. For all business/marketing inquiries regarding Boston Red Sox On SI, please reach out to Scott Neville: scott@moreviewsmedia.com

item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK -- Carson Benge had three hits to break Pete Alonso's Mets season rookie record, homering along with Francisco Alvarez as New York again prevented the Philadelphia Phillies from gaining ground in the National League wild card race with a 10-3 win Saturday.
Benge raised his hits total to 156, one more than Pete Alonso in 2019.
Alec Bohm had a pair of run-scoring singles and Bryce Harper delivered a sacrifice fly for the Phillies, who entered Saturday tied with the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres for the three NL wild cards, five games ahead of the Arizona Diamondbacks.
Alvarez's three-run home run off Andrew Painter (3-10) put the Mets ahead for good in the fifth.
Benge doffed his cap to an ovation from the crowd of 37,468 following the record-breaking hit, an RBI infield single in the eighth.
CUBS 5, REDS 2 Matthew Boyd ended a six-start winless streak, Dansby Swanson hit his first home run since coming off the injured list and visiting Chicago moved closer to its second consecutive playoff berth by beating Cincinnati. Michael Busch hit a tiebreaking home run off Nick Lodolo (3-6) in the sixth inning for a 3-2 lead, reaching 20 home runs for the third time in four seasons. Swanson added a ninth-inning drive against Zach McCambley, his first since Aug. 12.
NATIONALS 8, CARDINALS 5 (11) Washington scored four runs in the top of the 11th inning to break a 4-4 tie, then worked out of a bases-loaded jam with no outs in the bottom of the inning to get by host St. Louis. Jose Terra hit a two-run double to break the game open, giving the Nationals a 7-4 lead. Dylan Crews' sacrifice fly scored Jacob Young to make it 8-4. JJ Wetherholt hit an RBI single in the bottom of the inning to provide the final margin.
AMERICAN LEAGUE
RANGERS 6, BLUE JAYS 3 Five relievers held Toronto to six hits after Cal Quantrill left 12 pitches in because of right lat tightness, and Texas moved into sole possession of the AL West lead for the first time since late August with a win over visiting Toronto. Texas has won six of seven and moved a half-game ahead of Houston, which holds the tiebreaker. The Rangers have a winning record for the first time since before play on Aug. 11.
WHITE SOX 3, TIGERS 1 Sean Burke pitched six effective innings, Miguel Vargas homered and Chicago topped visiting Detroit. The White Sox dropped at least 101 games in each of the last three years. They could become the first big league team to make the playoffs after finishing with at least 100 losses in each of the previous two seasons. Burke (10-7) allowed one run and five hits in his second consecutive win. Grant Taylor got four outs for his 10th save.
RAYS 2, RED SOX 1 Richie Palacios dropped a fly ball into shallow right in the ninth inning to score Junior Caminero and give Tampa Bay a victory over visiting Boston. The Rays, who've won seven of their last eight, capitalized on two fortuitous bounces in the ninth. First, Caminero's foul popup bounced off the Tropicana Field catwalk and out of the reach of third baseman Caleb Durbin. Caminero then lined the next pitch from Garrett Whitlock (7-2) into left. Three batters later, after Chandler Simpson singled, Connor Wong's passed ball moved Caminero to third.
GUARDIANS 12, ATHLETICS 6 Angel Martínez homered from both sides of the plate and had his second career four-hit game, Chase DeLauter had a three-run home run, and host Cleveland remained in first place in the AL Central with a victory over the Athletics.
INTERLEAGUE
BRAVES 6, ASTROS 3 Ronald Acuna Jr. hit a go-ahead grand slam in the seventh inning, and visiting Atlanta beat Houston to drop the Astros out of the AL West lead. Trailing 2-1, Atlanta loaded the bases against AJ Blubaugh (5-3) and Acuna homered off Bryan Abreu for his second grand slam this season and the fifth of his big league career. Acuna singled and walked twice in his first three plate appearances. He has homered in three of his last four games.
BREWERS 1, ORIOLES 0 Visiting Milwaukee tied a team record with their 97th win of the season, beating Baltimore with the help of a fly ball lost in the sun by Orioles right fielder Rece Hinds. Hinds lost Joey Ortiz's fly ball in the sun in the second inning and tumbled to the ground, and Gary Sánchez hit into a run-scoring groundout.
PIRATES 6, ROYALS 5 Brandon Lowe hit a go-ahead two-run home run in the eighth to lift host Pittsburgh to a victory over Kansas City. Lowe jumped on a pitch from Steven Cruz (2-4) and sent it into the seats in right field for his 33rd home run of the season, the second-most by a player in their first year with the Pirates.
ROCKIES 5, MARINERS 3 Host Colorado used a four-run seventh inning to earn a victory over Seattle. The Mariners built a 3-0 lead, thanks to a two-run home run from Cal Raleigh in the first and a solo shot from Randy Arozarena in the third. Cole Carigg hit a two-run single in the seventh that gave the lead to Colorado, which got an RBI single from TJ Rumfield to tie the game at 3-3 earlier in the inning.
DIAMONDBACKS 5, YANKEES 3 Pavin Smith hit a two-run home run to right-center field in the bottom of the ninth inning to give host Arizona a victory over New York. Jordan Lawlar's triple in the bototm of the fifth scored Nolan Arenado to give Arizona a 2-1 lead, but Heliot Ramos hit a solo home run in the sixth to tie the game at 2-2. Austin Wells hit a home run later in the inning, giving New York the lead, but Arizona tied the game in the bottom of the inning when Ketel Marte scored on Corbin Carroll's sacrifice fly.

item.title: [nydailynews.com] Yankees’ division dreams hanging by a thread after walk-off loss: ‘It’s gonna be tough’
item.dc:creator: Gary Phillips
item.description: PHOENIX — Both the Yankees and Rays saw their respective games end in walk-off fashion on Saturday, but only one of the division rivals emerged victorious. It wasn’t the Yanks, who suffered a 5-3 loss to the Diamondbacks when Michael Fulmer surrendered a game-ending, two-run home to Pavin Smith with one out in the ninth inning. Aaron Boone said that he considered using Clarke Schmidt, one game back from Tommy John surgery, instead, but he went with the journeyman Fulmer because he’s had more exp
item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Both the Yankees and Rays saw their respective games end in walk-off fashion on Saturday, but only one of the division rivals emerged victorious.
It wasn’t the Yanks, who suffered a 5-3 loss to the Diamondbacks when Michael Fulmer surrendered a game-ending, two-run home to Pavin Smith with one out in the ninth inning. Aaron Boone said that he considered using Clarke Schmidt, one game back from Tommy John surgery, instead, but he went with the journeyman Fulmer because he’s had more experience in those situations.
“I just felt like Fulmer’s been in these spots and throwing the ball really well for us, and Smith got him there,” Boone said of the reliever, who has a 3.09 ERA this season.
Meanwhile, at Tropicana Field, the Rays pulled off a 2-1 win over the Red Sox thanks to a bloop single from Richie Palacios in the ninth. Tampa now has a five-game lead over the Yankees with just eight games left in the regular season.
The American League East foes will play four of those games against each other at Yankee Stadium from Sept. 22-24, starting with a doubleheader on Tuesday. Boone acknowledged that his club will probably have to sweep the Rays for a crack at a division title.
“We sweep, then it gets interesting,” the manager said with the Yankees’ postseason ticket already punched.
But the odds are already stacked against the Yankees with the team finishing its series in Arizona on Sunday. They entered Saturday with a just a 2.8% chance of winning the division, according to FanGraphs.
Making matters tougher is that the Rays, owners of the AL’s best record, currently lead the season series between the two teams, 6-3. There’s also the fact that the Yankees will be without Aaron Judge, who returned to the injured list with calf strain on Saturday.
“They’re playing tremendous baseball, so it’s tough to climb up in the standings when they keep winning,” Cody Bellinger said after going 0-for-4 on Saturday. “So mathematically, it’s pretty tough, but gotta keep on rolling.”
“We gotta go on a good run. It’s gonna be tough,” added Cam Schlittler, who allowed one earned run over six innings but committed a costly error on Saturday. “I think we’ve had opportunities all season to put ourselves ahead, and we haven’t done a great job with it. So there’s still a chance, but we gotta play our asses off a little bit.”
The good news for the Yankees is that their best starters are lined up to face the Rays. While they haven’t officially announced their probables for the series, it looks like Max Fried and Carlos Rodón will pitch the doubleheader before Gerrit Cole and Schlittler, the Cy Young frontrunner, close out the four-game set.
The Rays, however, are set to throw a few of their best with Drew Rasmussen, Nick Martinez, Ian Seymour and Freddy Peralta slotted for the highly-anticipated matchup.
While they’re not officially out of the division race yet, the likeliest scenario is that the Yankees end up hosting Boston in the Wild Card round for the second straight year. It is not where the team wants to end up after finishing 2025 with the same record as the Blue Jays but losing the season series tiebreaker, but Bellinger remained confident that the Yankees can still win their first title since 2009.
“Obviously, the goal is to win the division, rest your guys, get those extra off days,” he said. “That’s always goal No. 1. Ultimately, World Series champions have come out of the Wild Card.”

item.title: [courant.com] Dom Amore’s Sunday Read: Coach that launched Sun has his day; big skates to fill at UConn, and more

item.content:encoded:
Mike Thibault was with the Lakers during the early 1980s “Showtime” period, and he was with the Bulls when they drafted Michael Jordan. Then he moved around to different leagues, circumstances, and went back to the NBA as a Bucks assistant.
In 2003, he signed on to be the head coach the original Portland Fire of the WNBA, but Paul Allen, one of the richest men on earth, folded the franchise. Thibault learned the new Connecticut franchise wanted to talk to him, so he flew across the country, made the long drive in pitch darkness down Route 2 to find a shining city on hill.
“Then I look up and see the bright lights of the Mohegan Sun and the hotel and I thought, ‘Oh, this is different,'” Thibault said. “I stayed in the hotel the night before I was going to talk to them, and I went to the casino and won about $80, and the joke was, I told them, ‘well, if you don’t hire me, at least I got a little bit of your money.'”
All of Thibault’s quips landed and he became the first coach of the Connecticut Sun, leading them to the playoffs the first year, to the WNBA Finals in the second and third.
“It was pretty cool to be a part of that first non-NBA (affiliated) WNBA team,” he said, “having to fend for yourself without the backing of an NBA team in the market. I didn’t have trepidations about coaching women, I figured I would coach them just about the same way I coached men. I had been in the NBA, and then in the CBA, now the G League. I had never given much thought to coaching on the women’s side. But if I stayed in the NBA, I probably would have been a career assistant coach. I wanted to be a head coach. So I said, ‘why not?’ I was at a time in my life where if it wouldn’t be fatal (to my career) if it didn’t work out.”
The Sun made the playoffs in eight of their first 10 years, then let Thibault go after a loss in the conference finals in 2013. He went on to win the championship with Washington soon afterward, and he left The W as the winningest coach in its history, 379-289, though he has been passed by Cheryl Reeve. Now, as the Sun’s final season draws to a close, they will honor Mike Thibault during their second-to-last home game, the last name on the banner in the rafters of the arena noting those who were significant in the team’s history, a history both successful and yet oddly star-crossed.
“I was there 10 years and basically got fired in the midst of a good streak,” Thibault said, “and to be honored by the team, I don’t know that that usually happens in these situations. But I have such good memories of my time there. … The way the organization has handled a tough situation, with their “sunset season” theme, honoring former coaches and players, I think it’s very classy.”
Thibault, 75, now coaches Belgium’s national team, a commitment of 14-15 weeks per year, succeeding the final Sun coach, Rachid Meziane, in that position. Belgium finished fifth in the recent World Cup. Coaching in the WNBA in the summers gave Thibault a chance to settle in Connecticut and be around more for his son, Eric, now the coach of the Mystics, and his daughter, Carly Thibault-Dudonis, who is building an impressive legacy coaching Fairfield’s women. In The W, Mike Thibault was one of those who put a stamp on the league.
“Two teams folded that year, and one team moved to Connecticut,” he said. “But I knew the NBA’s commitment, and I knew David Stern’s commitment. so I didn’t worry about the WNBA not making it. Why not be a part of making something work? A lot of the coaches who came in at that time, Cheryl Reeve, Michael Cooper, Bill Laimbeer had a lasting impact. Before that, a lot of the coaches in the league were former college coaches and it was played more like the college game. The NBA influence brought a good blend, and it started to play more like a pro league.”
Today, he compares the league’s growth to the NBA in the 1980s, about 30 years into its history. “I think the game has gotten better, the talent is better, bigger, stronger, faster, better shooters, better athletes,” Thibault said. “It reminds me, I was in the NBA when it was about 30 years old and it started to take off during the 1980s with the talent level really high. The rules changes have allowed the game to be a little more free-flowing. It’s higher scoring, with the athlete taking over on the offensive side of the game. At times it gets physical, and it will be interesting to see how games are called during the playoffs. So TV is excited about it because it’s a more entertaining game.”
The Orlando franchise had been an underachiever, it was perceived. Thibault took over the roster in Connecticut and said his goal was to compete for the title, and he had Nykesha Sales and Rebecca Lobo for the chase.
“At my first press conference there were snickers when I said my first goal would be to play for a championship,” he said. “Everyone was like, ‘Dude!’ But you have to have that mindset going in. Then making the finals two years in a row. There were a lot of coulda, woulda, shoulda’s in both years. In 2006 I think we had our best team, but we were so injury-riddled and ground down when we got to the playoffs.”
In 2009, the Sun traded star Lindsay Whalen to the Lynx, a most painful moment for Thibault.
“I hated that I had to trade Lindsey Whalen,” Thibault said. “She was like a second daughter in my house. It was time because we couldn’t put enough players around her. But then we got Tina Charles and began the rebuild. We had the second youngest team in the league, the second lowest payroll, I was proud of that group. I got fired basically because I didn’t win a championship, even though we had committed two years earlier to the rebuild.”
Ultimately, Thibault jumped into a league struggling to survive and brought the credibility that helped stabilize a new franchise and the league — so in the larger picture he is more than just a “Sun Legend.” The Sun, purchased for $10 million in 2003, began making a profit in 2010, its location one of the reasons. Now it will go to Houston, having been sold for roughly $300 million.
The countdown is on for Sun’s final game in Connecticut is Sept. 24.
“I was sad,” Thibault said. “I understand it from a business standpoint, the league has changed, the money has changed. The salaries, the amenities you have to have, it’s hard to draw free agents, too. I felt bad for the fans more than anybody. … I thought Boston would have been a good compromise. The most disappointing thing was not winning a championship for our fans, the way they supported us. We gave it our best shot.”
More for your Sunday Read:
Filling iconic skates at UConn
Tia Chan was in goal for the UConn women’s hockey team for so long, playing at such a high level, one could almost call her an icon — rare for a college athlete. Now the Huskies, who reached the NCAA’s Elite Eight last year, have a strong cast of skaters led by high-scoring Claire Murdoch, but will be looking for the next goalie.
“We were worried when Elaine Chuli left (in 2016), we were worried when Morgan Fisher left (in 2020), we were worried when Annie Belanger left (2018),” coach Chris MacKenzie said. “I just think there is going to be someone who is going to step up. It’s happened enough over the 13 years we’ve been here, we’re going to need one of the three we have in there to step up.”
Senior Shannon Moran, freshman Ameilia Wilkinson and sophomore Taylor Belchetz are competing for the starting spot, and all three were expected to see action Saturday in the exhibition game vs. Quinnipiac, also an Elite Eight team, as was Yale.
Among the newcomers for MacKenzie are twin sisters Caileigh and Chelsea Tiller, who could have immediate impact as freshman. The UConn season begins at St. Cloud State Sept. 25.
Warnings from Wesleyan
Wesleyan football coach Dan DiCenso posted a video on social media this week in which he called out the New England Small School Athletic Conference for imposing roster limits on football.
“Football is the only sport in the NESAC with a mandated roster limit,” DiCenso begins. “If all the sports had a mandated roster limit and were making cuts, I would have no problem with it. So this week myself, and three or four schools in this situation, will cut kids from our team. This goes against all of Division III philosophy, all our NESCAC core values (to encourage participation in athletics).”
Wesleyan won the league title with no roster limits in 2024, and again when roster limits were put in for 2025, citing possible competitive advantages, capping at 84 players. DiCenso noted there are sports where there are large disparities between roster numbers.
“Common sense says, if there isn’t a roster limit in any other sport, why is there one in football?” he said. “… Do we want to talk about it? Or do we want to do something about it. I’m tired of having to meet with kids and not be able to give them a good reason why they can’t be on our team — just to practice and be there.”
Sunday short takes
*The Ivy League is moving its men’s basketball championship to Allentown, Pa., in 2028. Big mistake, I say. With the great, historic venues available in the league, most of which are easy for fans to reach, the Ivy’s four-team format was one of the most exciting and enjoyable of the conference tournaments. Messing with happy is never a good idea.
*Sports performance coaches should commission a study of the spotted lantern fly. Have you tried stepping on one? For a bug its size, it has to have the most explosive first step of any creature on earth.
*UConn men’s hockey coach Mike Cavanaugh filled out his staff with director of player development Ryan Shannon, Darien native, former Boston College and pro player and head coach at Taft School. Earlier, Sean Walsh, who also has pro playing experience, came from Alaska-Fairbanks to join Cavanaugh’s staff.
*Yard Goats manager Robinson Cancel will be a bench coach in the Mexican winter league with Tomateros de Culiacan. He will work with, and hopes to learn a lot from Lorenzo Bundy, a long-time MLB coach with a lot of pro managing experiencing.
*Jim Calhoun and his wife, Pat, will be honored by the University of Saint Joseph on Oct. 9 at the Connecticut Convention Center in Hartford. Tickets and details are available on USJ’s website at usj.edu/give/gala for: ‘A Legacy of Leadership. A Gala Honoring Pat and Jim Calhoun,’ the event to benefit the Calhoun Legacy Fund at USJ. Quite a few of Calhoun’s former players are expected.
*Art Shamsky, the 1969 Met, will be the guest at the Hartford World Series Club’s gathering on Sept. 23.
*Jackie Adams-Cheney, John Benoit, Dr. Kelly Harrigan, Robert Kalat, Sara Plourde-Zirkle, Tom Roberts, Don Sourcy and Jillian Sullivan are the Class of ’26 inductees for the Bristol Sports Hall of Fame. The induction ceremony will be Nov. 20 at the DoubleTree in Bristol, go to bshof.org for tickets and info.
*Dan Lauria, SCSU football player in the late 1960s, who turned to acting and gave us that quintessential 60s Dad on The Wonder Years, was inducted into the New Haven Gridiron Club Hall of Fame earlier this month.
Last word
*Cam Schlittler has been great for the Yankees, but any MVP talk is over the top. When starting pitchers threw complete games, they were viable candidates for both Cy Young and MVP, but it would be silly to give the MVP award to a five- or six-inning starter when there are sluggers like Yordan Alvarez flirting with the Triple Crown in Houston or Junior Caminero blowing past 40 homers for Tampa Bay.

item.content:encoded:
Palacios has RBI single in the 9th to Give the Rays a 2-1 Victory over the Red Sox
Richie Palacios dropped a fly ball into shallow right in the ninth inning to score Junior Caminero and give the Tampa Bay Rays a 2-1 victory over the Boston Red Sox on Saturday.
Tampa Bay, which has three walk-off wins on its current homestand, opened a five-game lead over the second-place New York Yankees in the AL East.
Prior to Palacios' single, the Rays were 0 for 17 with runners in scoring position over the first two games of the series. The postseason-bound Rays, who’ve won seven of their last eight, capitalized on two fortuitous bounces in the ninth.
First, Caminero’s foul popup bounced off the Tropicana Field catwalk and out of the reach of third baseman Caleb Durbin. Caminero then lined the next pitch from Garrett Whitlock (7-2) into left. Three batters later, after Chandler Simpson singled, Connor Wong's passed ball moved Caminero to third.
The Red Sox squandered a prime opportunity in the top of the ninth.
Facing closer Bryan Baker (4-2) in a tie game, Boston got Caleb Durbin's double and Jarren Duran's triple. However, Nick Fortes threw out Durbin stealing third and Caminero made a stellar play at third base to retire Isiah Kiner-Falefa, stranding Duran.
Boston also wasted a phenomenal effort from starter Brayan Bello, who matched a career high with 11 strikeouts. In eight innings, he allowed five hits, one run and no walks. Red Sox closer Aroldis Chapman (lat tightness) was unavailable.
The Red Sox took a 1-0 lead with bookend doubles from Durbin and Roman Anthony in the third inning. Trevor Story extended his hitting streak to 10 games with a sixth-inning single.
Jonathan Aranda tied it with an opposite-field solo homer on the first pitch of the Rays’ fourth.
The Rays are an MLB-best 25-14 in one-run games.
Up next
RHP Griffin Jax (7-10, 3.80 ERA) gets the nod for the Rays on Sunday in the series finale. Boston had not announced a starter.

item.title: [Audacy] Brayan Bello has suddenly become a potential key postseason piece
item.dc:creator: Rob Bradford

item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. - There was no celebration, but there was a revelation.
The Red Sox couldn't close the deal in securing a postseason berth, succumbing to a Rays 2-1 walk-off win at Tropicana Field on Saturday. But an interesting development emerged along the way. Brayan Bello is suddenly a potential huge part of the postseason solution.
The almost out-of-nowhere conversation about Bello's importance was given an enormous boost by one of the pitcher's best outings of his career. Not only did Bello hold the Rays to just one run over eight innings, but he also struck out 11 and walked no one.
Why was this even more impressive than simply the end-of-day box score? Because Bello managed all those punchouts, along with 17 whiffs, against a Rays team that has struck out fewer times than any club in baseball. No starting pitcher had managed double-digit strikeouts against Tampa Bay, with Toronto's Dylan Cease coming the closest with nine.
Bello matches his career high with 11 strikeouts! pic.twitter.com/NA2a2pDcAy
— Red Sox (@RedSox) September 19, 2026
The dominance was just what the doctor ordered for Bello and the Red Sox, even if starting a postseason game isn't in the righty's immediate future.
While there has been no announcement, it appears the Red Sox are lining up their wild-card rotation with Payton Tolle to pitch Game 1 against the Yankees, followed by Sonny Gray and then Ranger Suarez if Game 3 is needed in the best-of-three series. But that doesn't mean Bello can't have an impact on outcomes from late September into October.
Bello's fastball routinely sat at 97 mph, almost two mph above his season-average velocity. It was a fastball that got nine whiffs, with the Rays coming away with just four hard-hit balls all day.
"That was exceptional," Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy said. "By far and away, his best outing of the year, as good as I've seen him, so, I don't know what else to say, he was awesome. Really awesome."
Bello's appearance allowed for thoughts on what might be in store for his effectiveness out of the bullpen in high-leverage situations come Sept. 29. It has been well-documented what he can do as a reliever, posting a 1.98 ERA in 15 games out of the bullpen this season. But now we're not just talking about bulk roles or giving the Red Sox some length.
This version of Bello can absolutely be a late-inning, high-leverage weapon.
For instance, while we aren't sure of Aaron Judge's health heading into the postseason, if the Yankees' slugger does play, this might not be a bad reminder to put in your statistical back pocket: Judge is just 2-for-21 with eight strikeouts against Bello.
While some naysayers might point to the less-than-inspiring appearances Bello has turned in at Yankee Stadium as of late, including maybe his worst relief outing of the season at the end of August when he allowed four runs over 4 1/3 innings, or the 2 1/3-inning start in Game 2 of last season's wild card round. But before those two, the pitcher had been absolutely nails in the Bronx, totaling a 1.44 ERA in five starts.
Assuming their health is OK, the Red Sox will have Aroldis Chapman and Garrett Whitlock at the ready to help close out games. But with a week to go in the regular season, there is some uncertainty regarding the late-inning options. Saturday, Bello sure seemed like he was ready to help with that.
“For me, it's just showing the team that I'm ready for these kind of games,” Bello said. “Also, them giving me the opportunity to pitch today was a good step for that. And I thank them for giving me the confidence and the opportunity to start again.”

item.title: [bostonherald.com] Red Sox mailbag: Should Garrett Crochet, Tanner Houck be on playoff roster?
item.dc:creator: Mac Cerullo
item.description: Can you believe the playoffs are almost here? A week from today the Red Sox will wrap up their regular season, closing the book on what has been among the most unexpected, topsy turvy seasons we’ve ever seen. From there the playoffs await, and who knows what twists and turns may still be in store. But before we get there, what business is there left for the Red Sox to get squared away before Game 1 of the Wild Card series? We answer your questions in today’s Red Sox mailbag. Tanner Houck and Gar
item.content:encoded:
Can you believe the playoffs are almost here? A week from today the Red Sox will wrap up their regular season, closing the book on what has been among the most unexpected, topsy turvy seasons we’ve ever seen. From there the playoffs await, and who knows what twists and turns may still be in store.
But before we get there, what business is there left for the Red Sox to get squared away before Game 1 of the Wild Card series? We answer your questions in today’s Red Sox mailbag.
Tanner Houck and Garrett Crochet both appear close to ready to return. What is the chance that the Red Sox decide to put both of them on the postseason roster? Each feels like a high upside question mark but is it too risky relying on both of them to excel in limited roles? — Paul from Bluesky
If the Red Sox decide they’re ready I think there’s a great chance both pitch in the playoffs. The question of whether or not it’s too risky is valid, but the other factor to consider is would it be riskier to let an inferior arm take the mound at Yankee Stadium with the season on the line.
The nature of a best-of-three playoff series compared to a best-of-five or even a best-of-seven also makes the idea of loading up on short-inning relievers more attractive.
The Red Sox will only need three starting pitchers in the first round, presumably Sonny Gray, Ranger Suarez and Payton Tolle, in some order. That effectively frees up two additional bullpen spots, one of which I’m guessing will be filled by Jake Bennett as an emergency bulk man should the starter exit early due to injury or poor performance.
The back end of the bullpen is pretty much set in stone. If everyone is healthy and available it will be Aroldis Chapman, Garrett Whitlock, Erik Miller and Tyron Guerrero locking down the high leverage innings. But after that the Red Sox have some interesting decisions to make.
In one group you have the other short men, including Greg Weissert, Jovani Moran and Wyatt Olds. Then in the next group you have the longer men, including Patrick Sandoval, Brayan Bello, Alec Gamboa and Raymond Burgos. Finally, you have Crochet, Houck and Johan Oviedo, who has also begun a rehab assignment after missing nearly the entire season. What the Red Sox have to decide is which five of those 10 options give you the best chance to win?
I don’t think you can dispute that Crochet and Houck have the highest ceiling of that bunch, so if they’re good to go I don’t think the Red Sox will hesitate to give them the nod.
With Romy Gonzalez now hitting so well in Worcester, do you see him being put on the postseason roster as a lefty masher, and one of Isiah Kiner-Falefa, Andruw Monasterio or Jahmai Jones being left off? — @wcbosox on Bluesky
If the Red Sox believe Romy Gonzalez gives them the best chance to win in October, I feel like it would make sense for them to call him up and get him some looks at big league pitching over the last two weeks. You could make a great case that they should — he was batting .360 in 23 games since being optioned to Triple-A entering Friday — but if that doesn’t happen then that could be a sign the Red Sox don’t see him as part of the October plan.
Either way, the club has some tough decisions to make as far as constructing the bench goes.
Presuming that Ceddanne Rafaela returns from the IL without any issues and Willson Contreras isn’t sidelined by his hand injury, the Red Sox should enter the playoffs with a starting lineup featuring Adley Rutschman at catcher, Contreras, Nick Sogard, Trevor Story and Caleb Durbin across the infield, and an outfield of Rafaela, Wilyer Abreu, Roman Anthony and Jarren Duran, with one of Anthony or Duran presumably starting at designated hitter if a righty is on the mound.
That leaves four spots for Kiner-Falefa, Monasterio, Jones, Mickey Gasper, Connor Wong, Nate Eaton, Gonzalez and possibly Curtis Mead. For our purposes we can probably set aside Eaton, who will likely be optioned upon Rafaela’s activation, as well as Mead, who only just started swinging a light bat and won’t have the benefit of a rehab assignment prior to his return.
Let’s also set aside some of the more outside the box candidates like Braiden Ward, who has never appeared in a big league game but who may garner consideration as a late-inning pinch runner after stealing 60 bases at Triple-A.
One spot will go to a backup catcher, and while you could talk yourself into Gasper filling that role, Wong has the most familiarity with the pitching staff and the Red Sox would probably rather keep Gasper available as a pinch hitter without worrying about catching logistics.
How about the other three spots? Kiner-Falefa, Monasterio and Gonzalez are all versatile infield defenders who bat right-handed, so there’s some redundancy there. Jones also bats right-handed and could function as an emergency reserve outfielder in addition to his pinch hitter, and while Gasper is technically a switch hitter, his real value comes from the left side, where he’s crushed righties over the past month.
What’s going to happen? My guess is the bench will be Wong, Gasper, Jones and one of the three righty infielders. So to go back to your original question, could Gonzalez make the playoff roster over one of Kiner-Falefa, Monasterio or Jones? Yes, and in fact even if he doesn’t make the roster one of those guys could still wind up on the outside looking in.
If the playoffs started today who would be the starting second baseman? Also, what’s the long-term plan for that position? — Tom P.
If the playoffs started today I think Nick Sogard would be the clear choice to start at second base. He’s been an everyday player for the Red Sox since the end of July, and at a time where most of the offense has hit a skid Sogard has been a reliable contributor at the plate, batting .262 with five home runs and a .772 OPS entering the weekend since being called back up on July 29.
Long-term, the Red Sox have a couple of different candidates who could emerge in the coming years.
If he hadn’t broken his wrist in his team debut I think it’s safe to say Curtis Mead would have spent the past two months starting at second for the Red Sox. Prior to the trade he was in the midst of a breakout season with the Washington Nationals, and at only 25 years old there’s good reason to believe his best years are still ahead of him. Whether he returns in the playoffs or for the start of next season, Mead should have the best chance to claim second base for himself.
But outside of him, Sogard and perhaps Gonzalez or Anthony Seigler, there is one other wild card. That’s Franklin Arias.
The top Red Sox prospect is putting the finishing touches on a brilliant season, and if he continues to develop he should have a great chance of becoming a key building block, perhaps as soon as next year. With Story under contract for only one more season he will have an opportunity to slide right into the starting shortstop job entering 2028, but what if he proves he’s ready for primetime before that? In that case Arias might get an initial look at second, with Mead perhaps rotating between the designated hitter spot and occasionally giving Durbin and Contreras a breather at their corner infield positions.
Does MLB need to readjust its postseason schedule? The No. 2 or 3 team in the American League will be eliminated in a three-game series, meanwhile two teams that are barely .500 play each other in the first round. — Brandon C.
I like the idea that there should be a reward for winning your division. If you’re one of the top two division winners you get a first round bye, and if you’re the third division winner you at least get to host the best-of-three Wild Card series. I’m fine with that, even in a weird year like this where all of the American League’s best teams are in the same division and the other division leaders are mediocre at best.
But the problem is what happens afterwards. Like you said, the No. 2 and 3 teams in the AL are probably going to wind up being the Yankees and Red Sox, and whichever of those teams advances will have to play the No. 1 seeded Tampa Bay Rays. Meanwhile, all three teams on the other side of the bracket could potentially finish with worse records than anyone on the AL East side, and one of those clubs will be guaranteed a trip to the ALCS.
I think MLB could address this by reseeding after the Wild Card round. The top two division winners would still get home field advantage in their divisional series, but whichever team advancing out of the Wild Card round has the better record would be paired with the second division winner. So this year if the Red Sox beat the Yankees and let’s say the AL West champion wins their Wild Card series, the Red Sox would go on to play the AL Central champion instead of the Rays, while the AL West champion would get Tampa Bay even though they would have technically started the playoffs as the higher seed.
Most years it probably won’t make a huge difference, but reseeding ahead of the divisional round would strike a balance between preserving the incentives for winning your division while ensuring the bracket doesn’t become unbalanced.

item.content:encoded:
Sep 20, 2026, 12:47 AM ET
WEEI's Rob Bradford reports that it is "sure looking like" Boston Red Sox left-hander Payton Tolle has a "good shot" at pitching Game 1 of a wild-card series to kick off the postseason with the way the Red Sox are lining things up. It means that the 23-year-old southpaw will not get a start this weekend against the division-rival Tampa Bay Rays. The former second-rounder from TCU in 2024 has had a strong first full season in the big leagues with Boston in 2026, going 9-6 with a 3.02 ERA (3.04 FIP) and 1.07 WHIP with 166 strikeouts and 38 walks in 143 innings across his 25 starts. Another lefty, Patrick Sandoval, is now scheduled to make the start for the BoSox in the series finale in Tampa. Tolle allowed four earned runs in 5 2/3 innings against the Seattle Mariners on Aug. 31, but he has only given up one earned run with one walk and 19 punchouts in 12 innings across his last two starts against the Baltimore Orioles and Kansas City Royals in September.--Keith Hernandez
Source: WEEI - Rob Bradford
More Recent News
Xavier Edwards Leaves Early on Saturday With Thumb Discomfort


Keith Hernandez




Sep 20, 2026, 12:31 AM ET
Miami Marlins infielder Xavier Edwards (thumb) left Saturday night's game at Petco Park against the San Diego Padres early with discomfort in his left thumb, according to Christina De Nicola. The Marlins' training staff was checking Edwards' left hand out when he fouled a ball off in the seventh frame. It is worth noting that Edwards previously missed time this season with a sprained left thumb, which he might have aggravated on Saturday night. Before leaving the ballgame, Edwards went 0-for-3 with a walk and two strikeouts. He was replaced at the keystone in San Diego by Jared Serna. If the 27-year-old switch-hitting middle infielder did aggravate his left-thumb sprain, there is a good chance that he will not play again for the Marlins in the final week of the 2026 season. Edwards came into Wednesday's contest with a nice .282/.361/.373 slash line with a .733 OPS, a career-high six home runs, a career-high 52 RBI, 61 runs scored, and 21 stolen bases in 141 games played. He has stolen 20-plus bases in each of the last three seasons, including a career-high 31 back in 2024.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Christina De Nicola
Aaron Judge Hopes to be Back for Postseason, No Timetable Given


Keith Hernandez




Sep 20, 2026, 12:23 AM ET
New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge (calf) said on Saturday that his right-calf strain is in the soleus muscle, according to Bryan Hoch of MLB.com. However, Judge would not say what grade of strain his MRI exam revealed. "I'd like to be back by the postseason. That's definitely the plan. I got really no answers for you on any timeline or anything like that," Judge said. The New York Daily News' Gary Phillips reports that neither Judge nor manager Aaron Boone has shared much information on his injury, with the Yankees treating his calf strain like "classified CIA intel." "It doesn't matter what grade it is," Boone said. "We're at nine games left [in the season]." Because we have no idea of the exact severity of his calf injury, it is entirely plausible that Judge could miss most, or all, of any potential Yankees playoff run in October. Judge has been throwing, working out, and getting treatment, and he said he is "gonna do everything we can do to get back as soon as we can." Boone, though, merely said he is "hoping for the best." It will be difficult for the Yankees to go all the way if they do not get Judge back for the playoffs. It has been a frustrating year for the three-time MVP and all of his fantasy managers, as he has only played in 66 games due to a stress fracture in his rib, slashing .241/.360/.511 with 18 home runs, 41 RBI, 45 runs, and five steals.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Bryan Hoch
Roki Sasaki to Return Next Week


Andy Webb




Sep 19, 2026, 10:37 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Roki Sasaki (finger) will make his return to the mound next week during the series against the San Diego Padres, David Vassegh reports. Sasaki looked good during his side session on Wednesday, so the Dodgers have cleared him to get back on the mound. It doesn't sound like the Dodgers have decided whether Sasaki will start or come out of the bullpen during his outing against the Padres. The right-hander has been out since late August due to a finger blister. The expectation is that Sasaki will likely pitch in a bullpen role for the team during the postseason.--Andy Webb
Source: David Vassegh
Trey Yesavage to Start on Monday


Andy Webb




Sep 19, 2026, 10:31 PM ET
Toronto Blue Jays starting pitcher Trey Yesavage (knee) is scheduled to start against the Baltimore Orioles on Monday, Arden Zwelling of Sportsnet.ca reports. Yesavage has been out since August after having surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his right knee. He only made one rehab appearance at Triple-A Buffalo before getting cleared to pitch for the big league club. The Jays plan to have Yesavage pitch roughly three innings or around 45 to 50 pitches. Spencer Miles is expected to take over for the bulk of the innings after Yesavage is done. It'll be interesting to see if the Jays decide to shut down Yesavage if they do get eliminated from playoff contention. Until then, it sounds like the right-hander is going to contribute here soon.--Andy Webb
Source: Arden Zwelling
Cal Quantrill Removed with Lat Tightness


Andy Webb




Sep 19, 2026, 10:22 PM ET
Texas Rangers starting pitcher Cal Quantrill (lat) exited early during Saturday's outing against the Toronto Blue Jays. Quantrill was pulled out in the second inning due to right lat tightness, Kennedi Landry of MLB.com reports. He was able to record four outs before exiting this contest. Jordan Montgomery took over on the mound and threw 3.2 scoreless innings. Quantrill figures to undergo an MRI, so fantasy managers will likely have to wait for the results on that. Nathan Eovaldi could be asked to move back into the starting rotation if Quantrill is forced to miss time. UPDATE: The Dallas Morning News' Shawn McFarland reports that Quantrill will undergo an MRI exam on Sunday morning, per manager Skip Schumaker.--Andy Webb
Source: Kennedi Landry
Sep 19, 2026, 10:15 PM ET
New York Yankees outfielder Spencer Jones (foot) was not in the starting lineup ahead of Saturday's game against the Arizona Diamondbacks. The Yankees decided to rest Jones on Saturday due to left foot/heel soreness, according to Brendan Kuty of The Athletic. It sounds like a day-to-day issue, so the Yankees are just going to play it safe. Jones is 1-for-19 with nine strikeouts over his last four games, so he could probably use a day off to rest and reset. Jose Caballero takes over in center field for Saturday's game. Fantasy managers should check back ahead of Sunday's game for another update on Jones.--Andy Webb
Source: Brendan Kuty
Shohei Ohtani Takes Simulated At-Bats


Andy Webb




Sep 19, 2026, 10:05 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani (knee, biceps) has progressed to taking simulated at-bats off the team's pitching machine on Saturday, Jack Harris of the California Post reports. Ohtani was also able to run the bases as he works his way back from a biceps and knee issue. It's unclear if Ohtani will return when he's first eligible on Wednesday. The Dodgers have already clinched the postseason, so they don't exactly need to rush him back into the lineup. However, the Dodgers would probably like for Ohtani to play in a few regular-season games before the playoffs begin. Fantasy managers should check back for another update in a few days.--Andy Webb
Source: Jack Harris
Jac Caglianone Returning to Saturday's Lineup


Keith Hernandez




Sep 19, 2026, 5:54 PM ET
Kansas City Royals first baseman/outfielder Jac Caglianone (hand) is serving as the designated hitter and is batting third in Saturday's contest on the road against the Pittsburgh Pirates and right-hander Bubba Chandler, per MLB.com. Caglianone suffered a minor hand injury before Friday's series opener at PNC Park, but he is back in action on Saturday and should be returned to fantasy lineups against a right-hander, despite his cold streak of late. The 23-year-old former first-rounder has produced a .277/.328/.483 slash line with an .811 OPS, 23 home runs, 70 RBI, 66 runs scored, and six stolen bases in 484 at-bats in 2026 in his first full big-league season with the Royals. Cags was red-hot in August, slashing .411/.429/.684 with a 1.113 OPS, six home runs, eight doubles, 26 RBI, 17 runs scored, and three stolen bases in 24 games, but he has been banged up in September and has gone just 4-for-27 (.148) with zero homers, four RBI, one walk, and 11 strikeouts. He has never faced Chandler in the majors.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Sebastian Walcott to be Promoted to Triple-A


Keith Hernandez




Sep 19, 2026, 3:01 PM ET
Texas Rangers top infield prospect Sebastian Walcott is expected to be promoted to Triple-A Round Rock on Saturday, according to Kennedi Landry of MLB.com. Walcott will make his debut as the designated hitter on Saturday night. The No. 9 overall prospect in all of baseball, per MLB Pipeline, has only played in 39 games in the minors this year after having surgery on his UCL, but since returning, he has slashed .322/.398/.586 with nine home runs and 11 stolen bases in 37 games for Double-A Frisco. In a playoff series with the Rough Riders, Walcott went 4-for-11 with a homer and four stolen bases. Walcott is only 20 years old, but if he continues to ascend and looks good in spring training next year, he could push for an early-season MLB promotion for the Rangers. It is impossible to ignore his 40-homer upside at the shortstop position in fantasy baseball, which makes him a must-stash already in dynasty/keeper leagues.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Kennedi Landry
Orioles Shutting Ryan Helsley Down


Keith Hernandez




Sep 19, 2026, 1:40 PM ET
The Baltimore Orioles are shutting down right-handed reliever Ryan Helsley (elbow) for the rest of the season, general manager Mike Elias told Andy Kostka of The Baltimore Banner. The focus is on Helsley getting ready for next season. Elias said that Helsley is not dealing with a new injury, but the debate was over contracting his buildup timeline, and the O's opted against that. In related news, the Orioles reinstated right-handed reliever Felix Bautista (shoulder) from the 60-day injured list, and he will join the team's active roster for the first time since July of last year after he had surgery to fix a torn labrum and rotator cuff in his shoulder. Helsley's first year in Baltimore was a lost cause due to his elbow issues, as he was able to throw only 15 1/3 innings, going 0-4 with a 4.11 ERA, 1.43 WHIP, 21 strikeouts, and eight saves in 17 appearances. He will not be a lock to open the 2027 campaign as Baltimore's primary closer, especially with Bautista now back and healthy.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Baltimore Banner - Andy Kostka
Willson Contreras Still Out on Saturday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 19, 2026, 1:04 PM ET
Boston Red Sox first baseman Willson Contreras (hand) remains out of the team's starting lineup for Saturday's contest against the division-rival Tampa Bay Rays for the second straight day, per MLB.com. Nick Sogard will make another start at first base and will bat fifth against Rays right-hander Freddy Peralta. Contreras was diagnosed with a bruised right hand after leaving Thursday's game against the Texas Rangers after he was hit by a pitch. X-rays came back negative, though, so he is considered day-to-day and could make his return in Sunday's series finale in Tampa. Fantasy managers are hoping to get the 34-year-old Venezuelan back in their starting lineups as soon as possible, as the four-time All-Star has hit a career-high 27 home runs while driving in 81 runs in 129 games and 533 plate appearances in his first year with the club. Various injuries have limited Contreras to only four games so far in September, though, and he has gone 4-for-12 with a homer and two RBI.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Aroldis Chapman Won't Pitch This Weekend


Keith Hernandez




Sep 19, 2026, 11:07 AM ET
Boston Red Sox left-handed closer Aroldis Chapman (lat) felt some tightness in his lat while working out before Tuesday's game against the Texas Rangers and has not pitched since. Chapman said that he will not pitch this weekend against the division-rival Tampa Bay Rays, but he expects to return during the final homestand of the regular season, which starts on Tuesday, according to Ian Browne of MLB.com. The veteran southpaw downplayed the injury on Friday, saying that the Red Sox are being conservative and that he felt healthy enough to play catch before the series opener against the Rays, but the team told him not to. "I'm not worried at all," Chapman said. "From the first time I felt it to today, I feel very good. I was going to go out and throw, but the team wants to take it slow, and they want me to take my time." Fantasy managers will be without Chapman this weekend, but for championship matchups next week, he will hopefully be ready to return to ninth-inning duties. The 38-year-old has been excellent in 2026 in his second year in Boston, posting a 1.95 ERA with a 1.14 WHIP, 34 saves, and 68 strikeouts in 50 2/3 innings pitched. Right-hander Garrett Whitlock should handle a save situation this weekend if it arises in Tampa.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Ian Browne
Justin Verlander Throws Live Batting Practice


Dave Funnell




Sep 19, 2026, 10:03 AM ET
Detroit Tigers starting pitcher Justin Verlander (hamstring/hip) threw a one-inning, 20-pitch live batting practice session on Friday. The 43-year-old said that he felt great after this successful outing. This was yet another step in the right direction, as it was his first time throwing against live batters. What lies ahead in his progress remains to be seen, as the plan is for him to pitch one final time in his illustrious career on Saturday, September 26, against the Pittsburgh Pirates. Whether or not he is able to throw one inning or more remains questionable, but with him retiring after this season, chances are he will be healthy enough to make that appearance and cap off one of baseball's greatest careers. With 266 wins and 3,554 strikeouts over 21 seasons, the surefire Hall of Famer will be looking to finish his career where it started: in Detroit.--Dave Funnell - RotoBaller
Source: Chris McCosky
Trent Grisham Could Return This Season


Dave Funnell




Sep 19, 2026, 9:56 AM ET
New York Yankees outfielder Trent Grisham (hamstring) is pretty far into his recovery, two weeks after being placed on the 10-Day Injured List with a Grade 2 hamstring strain. Manager Aaron Boone reiterated that a return for him "could be in play" for the latter part of the season. It was also mentioned that when he does return, the Yankees would need to decide between him and Spencer Jones to play center field. This could complicate things for both players, as there could be some sort of platoon involving the two, diminishing their fantasy value down the stretch. Either way, the Yankees will be looking to solidify their lineup for the playoffs, and Grisham's fantasy value is very limited down the stretch, with or without a return before the playoffs.--Dave Funnell - RotoBaller
Source: Brendan Kuty - The Athletic
Tristan Peters Dealing With Multiple Injuries


Dave Funnell




Sep 19, 2026, 9:39 AM ET
Chicago White Sox outfielder Tristan Peters (rib/shoulder) crashed into the wall during Friday's game while trying to catch a fly ball in the outfield. He exited the game with contusions to both his ribs and shoulders, and Braden Montgomery took his place in the outfield. The good news is that he is listed as day-to-day and has no head injury, which was the initial concern at the time of impact. It's unclear if he will miss any time before returning, but with the White Sox in the middle of a divisional race, they may need his help sooner rather than later. The 26-year-old is hitting .272 on the season with 12 home runs and eight stolen bases, and is worth rostering in deep leagues.--Dave Funnell - RotoBaller
Source: Chicago White Sox
Justin Steele Completes Two-Inning Rehab Outing


Dave Funnell




Sep 19, 2026, 9:30 AM ET
Chicago Cubs pitcher Justin Steele (elbow) threw a 33-pitch, two-inning rehab outing on Friday for the Triple-A Iowa Cubs. This was his fifth appearance since beginning his rehab assignment and the fourth that has been two innings in length. Arguably his most impressive outing yet, Steele walked the first batter of the game before striking out the side. He would finish with five strikeouts in total while not allowing a hit. While the velocity on his fastball sat at 90.2 miles per hour, it was his slider that impressed the most, generating four whiffs. It's unclear what lies ahead for him, as the Cubs are in the middle of a race for the Wild Card. While they have a comfortable lead on the teams chasing them, they do need to prepare for the postseason, and Steele returning to the Cubs may not be in the cards. What's clear is that he is feeling much better than he has in quite some time, and any return to the Cubs would likely be for a peace-of-mind appearance to allow him to enter the postseason on a healthy note, giving him the opportunity to work on coming back even stronger next spring. Fantasy managers should not expect much from him down the stretch, but those in dynasty leagues should take note and add him while they can.--Dave Funnell - RotoBaller
Source: Jason Kempf
Bryce Eldridge Expected to Play on Saturday


Dave Funnell




Sep 19, 2026, 9:17 AM ET
San Francisco Giants first baseman Bryce Eldridge (head) was scratched from the lineup on Friday after cutting his head at the team's hotel before opening pitch. Manager Tony Vitello said that he expects the 21-year-old slugger to play on Saturday, noting that the injury doesn't appear to have any long-term ramifications. In his place on Friday, Brett Harris took over at first base and would likely do the same on Saturday should any unforeseen complications arise. That being said, it would appear that the promising rookie is set to take the field and try to finish what should be considered a successful debut season. Over 107 games played, Eldridge has hit 17 home runs and collected 57 runs batted in, all while posting a robust .269/.364/.461 slash line. Fantasy baseball managers should insert him back into their lineups once he's healthy and leave him there through the end of the 2026 season.--Dave Funnell - RotoBaller
Source: Justice delos Santos
Sep 18, 2026, 10:02 PM ET
San Francisco Giants starting pitcher Logan Webb (finger) was placed on the 15-day injured list on Friday, Alex Pavlovic of NBC Sports Bay Area reports. Webb will see his regular season come to an end due to a right middle finger blister. The Giants were reportedly considering shutting down Webb after his latest start. The right-hander has allowed 16 earned runs over his last three starts. He'll now get plenty of time to heal his injury and prepare for the 2027 season. He'll finish the season with a 4.31 ERA, 1.17 WHIP, and a 134/41 K/BB ratio in 27 starts.--Andy Webb
Source: Alex Pavlovic
Sep 18, 2026, 9:52 PM ET
Toronto Blue Jays manager John Schneider said on Friday that it would be tough for starting pitcher Shane Bieber (shoulder) to return before the end of the regular season, Hazel Mae of Sportsnet reports. Bieber is scheduled to throw a side session on Saturday, so the Jays should have a better idea about his status after that. The right-hander has been sidelined since late August due to shoulder inflammation. He probably doesn't have time to build up into a starter again, so if he returns, Bieber would likely pitch in a limited role. Fantasy managers in redraft formats are probably safe to move on at this point.--Andy Webb
Source: Hazel Mae
Sep 18, 2026, 9:33 PM ET
Pittsburgh Pirates starting pitcher Braxton Ashcraft (arm) is unlikely to return to the mound this season, Kevin Gorman of TribLive.com reports. Ashcraft appears to be making progress as he was able to play catch from 90 feet on Friday. Despite that, Ashcraft is unlikely to make enough progress to get back on the mound before the end of the regular season. Ashcraft has been out since early September due to right arm discomfort. Ashcraft is probably done for the year, but he did post a breakout campaign for the Pirates this season. Across 28 starts, Ashcraft posted a 3.65 ERA, 1.09 WHIP, and a 173/35 K/BB ratio across 165.1 innings of work.--Andy Webb
Source: Kevin Gorman

item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — Richie Palacios dropped a blooper into shallow right in the ninth inning to score Junior Caminero and give the Tampa Bay Rays a 2-1 victory over the Boston Red Sox on Saturday.
Tampa Bay, which has three walk-off wins on its current homestand, lowered its magic number to clinch the AL East to five games. The second-place Yankees are in Arizona on Saturday night.
Prior to Palacios’ single, the Rays were 0 for 17 with runners in scoring position over the first two games of the series. The postseason-bound Rays, who’ve won seven of their last eight, capitalized on two fortuitous bounces in the ninth.
First, Caminero’s foul popup bounced off the Tropicana Field catwalk and out of the reach of third baseman Caleb Durbin. Caminero then lined the next pitch from Garrett Whitlock (7-2) into left. Three batters later, after Chandler Simpson singled, Connor Wong’s passed ball moved Caminero to third.
Bidding to clinch a wild-card berth, the Red Sox squandered a prime opportunity in the top of the ninth.
Facing closer Bryan Baker (4-2) in a tie game, Boston got a double from Caleb Durbin and a triple from Jarren Duran. However, Nick Fortes threw out Durbin stealing third before Duran’s triple, and Caminero made a stellar play at third base to retire Isiah Kiner-Falefa, stranding Duran.
Boston also wasted a phenomenal effort from starter Brayan Bello, who matched a career high with 11 strikeouts. In eight innings, he allowed five hits, one run and no walks. Red Sox closer Aroldis Chapman (lat tightness) was unavailable.
The Red Sox took a 1-0 lead with doubles from Durbin and Roman Anthony in the third inning. Trevor Story extended his hitting streak to 10 games with a sixth-inning single.
Jonathan Aranda tied it with an opposite-field solo homer on the first pitch of the Rays’ fourth.
The Rays are an MLB-best 25-14 in one-run games.
Boston could have clinched a playoff berth with a win combined with a loss by either the Rangers or Astros. Both of those teams were seven games behind the Red Sox with eight games remaining entering Saturday.
UP NEXT
Right-hander Griffin Jax (7-10, 3.80 ERA) gets the nod for the Rays on Sunday in the series finale. Boston had not announced a starter.

item.title: [Boston Sports Journal] Red Sox denied playoff clincher as Rays walk off Garrett Whitlock, 2-1
item.dc:creator: Chris Henrique
item.description: The Red Sox were one swing away from punching their ticket to October. Instead, they’ll have to wait at least one more day. Richie Palacios dumped a walk-off single into right field off Garrett Whitlock in the bottom of the ninth inning Saturday, lifting the Rays to a 2-1 win over the Red Sox at Tropicana Field and preventing Boston from clinching a postseason berth. The Rays pieced together three singles against Whitlock in the ninth after the teams entered the inning tied at 1. Boston had oppo
item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox were one swing away from punching their ticket to October. Instead, they’ll have to wait at least one more day.
Richie Palacios dumped a walk-off single into right field off Garrett Whitlock in the bottom of the ninth inning Saturday, lifting the Rays to a 2-1 win over the Red Sox at Tropicana Field and preventing Boston from clinching a postseason berth.
The Rays pieced together three singles against Whitlock in the ninth after the teams entered the inning tied at 1. Boston had opportunities to push across the go-ahead run in the later innings but couldn’t capitalize, wasting an outstanding performance from Brayan Bello.
Bello turned in arguably his most impressive start of the season, allowing just one run on five hits over eight innings while striking out 11 to match his career high.
“That was exceptional,” Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy told reporters following the game. “By far and away his best outing of the year. As good as I’ve seen him. So, I don’t know what else to say. He was awesome, really awesome.”
It marked the second consecutive scoreless start for Bello, but Saturday’s outing was far more dominant than his previous one. Against the Angels at Fenway Park, Bello navigated almost constant traffic, allowing four hits and two walks while needing 103 pitches to complete five innings.
Bello needed just 55 pitches to complete his first five innings and kept the Rays off balance throughout the afternoon. He allowed only one run, a Jonathan Aranda’s solo homer leading off the fourth, and gave the Red Sox exactly what they needed with two of their most important late-inning relievers unavailable.
“I just felt confident attacking the zone,” Bello told reporters via team translator.
Bello isn’t expected to start in the Wild Card Series, but his recent performances have provided a reminder of the value he could offer in October. After an uneven season that eventually resulted in a move to the bullpen, he has reestablished himself as someone Tracy can trust in a meaningful spot.
Aranda’s homer was notable for another reason. It was the first home run Bello had allowed since July 12, the final game before the All-Star break, snapping a homerless stretch of roughly 42 innings. Much of that work came in relief, often following an opener, but going more than two months without surrendering a homer remains an impressive run.
“For me, it’s just showing the team that I’m ready for this kind of games,” Bello added.
For the second straight game, Roman Anthony provided Boston with some early offense.
After leading off Friday’s victory with a 438-foot homer, Anthony delivered again in the third inning Saturday. Caleb Durbin opened the inning with a double before Anthony sliced an RBI double into left-center to give Boston a 1-0 lead.
The productive at-bats are an encouraging development for Anthony after his recent slump. With the postseason just over a week away, the rookie is beginning to show signs of heating up at the right time.
Durbin may be coming out of a slump of his own.
After collecting two hits in Friday’s series opener, Durbin added two more Saturday, both sharply hit doubles. His offensive turnaround earlier this season coincided with Boston’s surge up the standings, and another hot stretch would add length to the lineup and provide another productive right-handed bat heading into October.
